1	# marvin — System Specification
2	
3	> **Read this first** for any non-trivial marvin task. The journal ([`journal.md`](journal.md)) is the running diary of decisions and work-in-progress; this spec is the durable description of *what marvin is*. When the two disagree, fix the spec.
4	
5	**Status:** in-progress draft. Sections that are settled are marked ✅; sections that depend on open architectural questions are marked 🚧 and link to the relevant entries in §9.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Purpose & scope
10	
11	### 1.1 What marvin is
12	
13	marvin is the firmware running on a **SAM9X75 Curiosity** board. Its job, in the guitar-playing-robot system, is to:
14	
15	1. Capture live HDMI video of a Guitar Hero / Rock Band game from a Nintendo Wii.
16	2. Run computer-vision note detection on the captured frames.
17	3. Decide *what* to play and *when* (chord grouping, fret-early timing, strum scheduling).
18	4. Send the corresponding fret/strum commands to the actuator controller (the **fretboard** MCU).
19	5. Provide an on-device operator UI (10.1″ LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch) for live view, calibration, mode selection, logs.
20	6. Produce **reference data** — annotated frames + detector state — for off-board use (training low-fidelity detectors, side-by-side detector comparison, replay).
21	7. **Observe game state from the screen** — recognize current menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score-summary contexts via CV, expose high-level control verbs ("start single-player playthrough of song X", "advance menu", "exit to main menu") that translate into fret/strum command sequences sent through the same fretboard link.
22	
23	In short: marvin is the runtime brain *and* the reference-detector data source for the project.
24	
25	### 1.2 What marvin is *not*
26	
27	- **Not the actuator.** Physical fret/strum GPIO drive lives on the fretboard MCU. marvin sends bitmask commands; fretboard converts them to button presses.
28	- **Not a sensor / detection-only device.** marvin owns timing and command emission. It is not a passive vision peripheral that some other host orchestrates.
29	- **Not a router for a PC.** The previous PC-based architecture (Elgato + OpenCV + USB to a Pi) is retired. marvin replaces the PC in the runtime path.
30	- **Not a generic camera platform.** The video source is a fixed HDMI signal from a game console. Suggestions like "just use a USB webcam" or "output to HDMI directly" miss the point.
31	
32	### 1.3 North-star one-paragraph summary
33	
34	A SAM9X75 captures Wii HDMI video at 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz over a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 → ISC path into DDR (BGR888 packed, 3 B/pixel). It runs reference-quality CV note detection on those frames, fuses with ADC-based detection ingested from a fretboard MCU over a FLEXCOM2 UART link, schedules chord/strum commands through a low-latency timing pipeline, sends commands back to the fretboard, drives an operator UI on a 10.1″ LVDS panel, and exports a compressed reference-data stream so that lighter-weight detectors (today: fretboard's phototransistors; future: an Edge AI MCU) can be trained against marvin's ground truth.
35

123	### 2.2 Who owns what
124	
125	| Concern | Owner | Notes |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| HDMI capture into memory | marvin | TC358743 + CSI-2 + ISC; 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz, BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel). |
128	| Reference-quality CV note detection | marvin | Ground truth; multiple algorithms may coexist on the bus. |
129	| ADC-based note detection | fretboard → marvin | fretboard scans 5 phototransistors @ 240 Hz, streams raw values; marvin runs the detector logic. |
130	| Detector-state fusion / arbitration | marvin | One canonical detector-state bus; the active source feeds the timing pipeline. |
131	| Chord-window FIFO + strum scheduling | marvin | Open Q4: stays on marvin (centralized) vs migrates to fretboard. Default: marvin. |
132	| Fret/strum GPIO output | fretboard | Open-drain pin drive only; receives a bitmask over UART. |
133	| Operator UI (live view, calibration, modes, logs) | marvin | 10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch. Open Q5: Legato vs custom. |
134	| Reference-data recording & export | marvin | Compressed/derived format; transport TBD (open Q1/Q2). |
135	| Game-state observation (menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score) | marvin | CV on captured frames; emits typed game-state events on its own bus. §4.8. |
136	| Game catalog + menu metadata (song list, menu graph, recognized icons) | marvin | Compile-time tables and/or SD-card JSON. Drives the recognizer and the navigator. §4.8. |
137	| High-level game control (e.g., "start single-player song X") | marvin | Translates verbs into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link as gameplay commands. §4.8. |
138	| Calibration / tuning UI authoring | dev PC (fret-tuner) | Optional; not required at runtime. Open Q7: long-term fate. |
139	| Training data ingest / replay analysis | dev PC | Off-band consumer of marvin's reference-data export. |
140	
141	### 2.3 Data flow at a glance
142	
143	1. **Frame ready** — ISC writes a BGR888 packed frame to DDR; the video task notifies subscribers.
144	2. **CV detect** — one or more CV detectors read the frame and emit detector-state events.
145	3. **ADC ingest** — a UART task receives raw ADC samples from the fretboard and runs an ADC detector that emits detector-state events on the same bus.
146	4. **Arbitrate** — the timing pipeline picks the active detector (or fuses), maintains the chord-accumulation window, and pushes finished chords onto its FIFO.
147	5. **Schedule** — the FIFO emits fret-assert and strum-pulse commands at the correct ticks.
148	6. **Send** — commands are encoded and transmitted to the fretboard over UART.
149	7. **Display** — the captured frame is composited with overlays (sensor crosshairs, detector outputs, chord state, latency markers) and shown on the LVDS panel.
150	8. **Record** (optional) — when recording is enabled, a derived/compressed reference-data record (frame epoch + detector state + raw ADC + emitted commands) is buffered and exported via the chosen transport.
151	
152	### 2.4 Latency budget (target, end-to-end)
153	
154	| Stage | Budget | Notes |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| HDMI source → DDR (capture) | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame @ 60 Hz; bounded by capture pipeline. |
157	| Detect on frame | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame budget for CV; ADC path is separate and faster. |
158	| Timing pipeline → command emit | latency dominated by `STRUM_DELAY_MS` (≈ 200 ms) — intentional, not waste; compensates for sensor placement above strike line. |
159	| UART command → fretboard GPIO | ≤ 5 ms | Short fixed-format frame at ≥ 115 200 Bd. |
160	| Total user-visible latency | ≈ 200–250 ms | Tunable via `STRUM_DELAY_MS`, set per-game by calibration. |
161	
162	The dominant fixed delay (`STRUM_DELAY_MS`) exists by design — the camera sees notes before they reach the strike line. Capture + detect + UART jitter is what we actually budget against.

202	
203	## 4. Subsystems
204	
205	### 4.1 Video capture & display ✅
206	
207	Working end-to-end. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) and [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) for register-level detail. The video task (`video.c`, FreeRTOS) owns the capture pipeline and a frame queue that other tasks subscribe to. Display intent and capture intent are decoupled (commit `e28c497`); a software scaler can be inserted between capture and display when source ≠ panel native.
208	
209	**What this subsystem owns:**
210	- TC358743 init, source detection, EDID, format negotiation.
211	- ISC DMA configuration and frame buffer rotation in DDR.
212	- XLCDC overlay window placement (pillarbox/letterbox) for the active source.
213	- Frame-ready notification to subscribers (CV detect, recording, UI overlay).
214	
215	**What it doesn't own:**
216	- CV processing (§4.2).
217	- Recording / export (§4.6).
218	- UI widgets / chrome (§4.5) — only the pixel composition for the live-view layer.
219	
220	### 4.2 CV detection pipeline + detector-state bus 🚧
221	
222	#### 4.2.1 Role
223	
224	This is what makes marvin the *reference detector*. It runs computer-vision note detection on captured frames and publishes a structured detector-state record per frame onto a shared bus. Other detectors (fretboard ADC; future Edge-AI unit) publish onto the same bus. The timing pipeline (§4.4) consumes the bus.
225	
226	#### 4.2.2 Detector model
227	
228	A **detector** is anything that turns observation data into a `detector_state_t` event. marvin will host at least:
229	
230	- `cv_marvin_v1` — the reference vision detector. Reads RGB888-packed (3 B/pixel) frames from the video frame queue; emits one `detector_state_t` per frame.
231	- `adc_fretboard` — runs on top of raw ADC samples streamed from the fretboard MCU (§4.3); emits `detector_state_t` events at the fretboard's 240 Hz rate.
232	
233	Future detectors may include alternate CV algorithms running in parallel for comparison, or off-board detectors (Edge-AI MCU) feeding state in over UART/Ethernet.
234	
235	#### 4.2.3 detector_state record (canonical shape)
236	
237	```
238	typedef struct {
239	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync token (§4.6.4)
240	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    // monotonic, marvin-local
241	    uint8_t  detector_id;     // 0=cv_marvin_v1, 1=adc_fretboard, ...
242	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
243	    struct {
244	        uint8_t  pressed;     // 0/1 hard call
245	        uint16_t confidence;  // 0..65535, detector-defined
246	        uint16_t raw_value;   // detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc.
247	    } fret[5];                // FRET_GREEN..FRET_ORANGE
248	} detector_state_t;
249	```
250	
251	Fields are fixed-width, naturally aligned, little-endian — this is also the on-disk record layout for the state log (§4.6.5). `frame_epoch` is the master clock for cross-detector and cross-recording sync.
252	
253	#### 4.2.4 Bus mechanics
254	
255	- A single FreeRTOS queue (`xDetectorStateQueue`) carries `detector_state_t` records, one entry per detector emit.
256	- The timing pipeline task (§4.4) is the sole consumer.
257	- The recording task (§4.6) snoops the queue via a side-channel: each producer publishes simultaneously to the timing-pipeline queue and to a recording stream buffer. (Single producer→multiple consumers is implemented by tee'ing inside each detector, not by a broker; keeps queue semantics blocking and simple.)
258	- Detectors run on their own FreeRTOS tasks (one per detector instance) so a slow detector cannot stall the frame pipeline.
259	
260	#### 4.2.5 Reference-detector responsibilities
261	
262	`cv_marvin_v1` is a *first-class* subsystem, not a debug aid. Its detector state is the ground-truth label for any reference-data recording (§4.6). Implications:
263	
264	- Algorithm changes are versioned (`cv_marvin_v1`, `cv_marvin_v2`, …). The version is stamped into recordings so training data stays attributable.
265	- Calibration (sensor/strike-line ROIs in pixel space) is stored in the system config (§4.7) and reproducibly applied at startup.
266	- The detector must run within one frame-time (≤ 16.7 ms) on Cortex-A5 — concrete algorithm choice is a future decision, but the budget is set.
267	
268	#### 4.2.6 Open questions surfaced here
269	
270	- Initial CV algorithm — pixel-mean threshold per ROI, edge-trough, optical-flow-based, or learned. (Defer; bring up the simplest first to validate end-to-end.)
271	- ADC-detector logic location — port `fretboard/fret_button.c`'s detection (hysteresis edges) into marvin (`adc_fretboard` runs on raw samples), or have fretboard pre-process and stream edges. (Default: marvin runs the detector on raw samples; fretboard stays dumb.)
272	
273	### 4.3 Fretboard link ✅
274	
275	Direct **FLEXCOM1 USART** link between marvin and the fretboard MCU — a plain UART wire, no USB. marvin's `PA28` (FLEXCOM1_IO0, `GUITAR_TX`) and `PA29` (FLEXCOM1_IO1, `GUITAR_RX`) connect to the fretboard's SERCOM1 (`PB01` RX / `PB00` TX). Both ends run **500 000 baud, 8N1**. The FLEXCOM1 USART runs in Harmony ring-buffer mode so RX never drops bytes between reads. (Was FLEXCOM2 until the console moved onto FLEXCOM2 — see §4.9.)
276	
277	- **Marvin → fretboard:** command bitmask (which frets to assert + strum direction). 1-byte bitmask, no framing. `fretboard_link_task` writes the latest mask via `FLEXCOM1_USART_Write`.
278	- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 240 Hz, in a 17-byte start/end-bracketed frame (`0x03 … 0xFC`, with `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`). The FLEXCOM1 RX ring fills continuously from its ISR; a persistent read-threshold notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which drains the ring, resyncs on the frame markers, and republishes each valid frame as a `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` perf-log record (default-disabled, host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`). This is the on-board capture path until the SD-card recorder lands; it's also the substrate for the future `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2).
279	- **Standalone fallback:** when marvin's timing pipeline is disabled (see §4.4 and §6), the fretboard runs its own existing chord FIFO (`fret_button.c`) and continues to stream ADC + emitted-command telemetry to marvin for capture/display.
280	
281	### 4.4 Timing pipeline 🚧
282	
283	Centralized on marvin by default. Owns:
284	
285	- Chord-accumulation window (`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` ≈ 20–40 ms).
286	- Pending-chord FIFO with per-chord `press_at` / `strum_at` ticks.
287	- Per-fret release scheduling.
288	- Strum direction alternation and pulse generation.
289	- `STRUM_DELAY_MS` / `FRET_EARLY_MS` / `STRUM_PULSE_MS` constants — initial values port from `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md` and `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`.
290	
291	**Disable / handoff mode:** an operator-mode toggle (§6) deactivates marvin's pipeline. fretboard then runs its own existing pipeline; marvin still ingests ADC + emitted-command telemetry for recording/display, but does not emit commands.
292	
293	### 4.5 UI / operator surface 🚧
294	
295	10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch. Functional surfaces required:
296	
297	- Live game view (capture composited with detector overlays — sensor crosshairs, detection events, latency markers).
298	- Calibration / tuning (per-fret ROI placement, threshold values, timing constants).
299	- Mode + run controls (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record).
300	- Logs / history / stats (recent commands, miss/hit counts, dropped frames).
301	
302	**UI framework — open Q5.** Legato is already pulled in for capture init and could absorb the operator UI directly (heavy but in-tree). Alternative: a lightweight custom widget layer over GFX2D / direct framebuffer composition. Decision deferred until we attempt the first non-trivial screen (calibration overlay).
303	
304	### 4.6 Reference-data recording & export 🚧
305	
306	#### 4.6.1 Goals (in priority order)
307	
308	1. **Edge-AI training data** — produce labelled frames + ground-truth detector state suitable for training low-fidelity detectors (fretboard's photo-detector logic; future Edge-AI MCU).
309	2. **Replay / sanity check** — let the user (offline) scrub through a recorded session to investigate misses.
310	3. **Multi-detector sync** — independent detectors (fretboard ADC, future Edge-AI) record their own data alongside marvin's; everyone sync's on a shared frame epoch.
311	
312	Live off-device streaming for side-by-side comparison is *not* on the MVP critical path.
313	
314	#### 4.6.2 Transport — SD card
315	
316	Recordings are persisted to an SD card via SDMMC + a simple filesystem (FAT32 via Harmony's FILE_SYSTEM service). The card is removed and read on a workstation; no live network path is required for MVP.
317	
318	Bandwidth ceiling: SDMMC sustained write ≥ 5 MB/s on Class-10 cards is reliably achievable. The recording format below is sized to land well below that.
319	
320	#### 4.6.3 Format — detector-state + sparse keyframes
321	
322	A recording is a **directory** on the SD card, containing:
323	
324	```
325	recordings/
326	└── 2026-05-20T14-32-08/
327	    ├── manifest.json          // session metadata, calibration snapshot, detector versions
328	    ├── state.bin              // dense detector_state_t records, all detectors, all frames
329	    ├── commands.bin           // emitted fret/strum commands with frame_epoch
330	    ├── adc_raw.bin            // raw fretboard ADC stream with frame_epoch interleave
331	    └── keyframes/
332	        ├── 000000.bgr         // raw BGR888 keyframe (no encoder), filename = frame_epoch
333	        ├── 000060.bgr
334	        └── ...
335	```
336	
337	- **`state.bin`** — append-only, fixed-size `detector_state_t` records (§4.2.3). At 60 Hz × 2 detectors × ~28 B = ~3.4 KB/s. Trivial.
338	- **`commands.bin`** — fret/strum bitmask + direction + emit timestamp + frame_epoch, ~16 B per emit. Sparse.
339	- **`adc_raw.bin`** — fretboard 17-byte frames at 240 Hz with `frame_epoch` annotation = ~4.1 KB/s. Modest. Until the SD recorder lands, the same data is available live as `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` records (28 B framed) in any marvin-perf capture (default-disabled; enable with `set-mask`).
340	- **Keyframes** — raw BGR888 packed dump every N captured frames. At 720×480 × 3 B = 1.04 MB/keyframe. Default cadence: **1 keyframe per second** (60-frame stride) → 1.04 MB/s sustained. Configurable (every 30 / 60 / 120 / 600 frames). At 1 fps a 5-minute session is ~312 MB — comfortable on any modern SD card.
341	- No software JPEG / video encode. SAM9X75 has no hardware JPEG; CPU encode at 60 fps is infeasible. Keyframes stay raw; offline tools can transcode if desired.
342	
343	Filename convention: directory name is ISO-8601 timestamp at session start (UTC); keyframe filenames are zero-padded `frame_epoch` so chronological order matches lexical order.
344	
345	#### 4.6.4 Sync token — `frame_epoch`
346	
347	A 32-bit counter incremented by the video task on every captured ISC frame (rolls over after ~830 days @ 60 Hz). Every record in a session — `state.bin`, `commands.bin`, `adc_raw.bin`, keyframe filenames, off-board detector data — is keyed by `frame_epoch`. This is the master clock for the entire system, including any later-added detectors that record independently and need to align their data with marvin's.
348	
349	For records that don't fall on a frame boundary (ADC samples emitted between video frames), the most-recent `frame_epoch` is used and the sub-frame offset is captured by `timestamp_us`.
350	
351	#### 4.6.5 manifest.json
352	
353	Minimum fields:
354	
355	```json
356	{
357	  "schema_version": 1,
358	  "session_started_utc": "2026-05-20T14:32:08Z",
359	  "marvin_firmware_git": "<hash>",
360	  "capture": { "width": 720, "height": 480, "fps": 60, "format": "BGR888" },
361	  "keyframe_stride_frames": 60,
362	  "detectors": [
363	    { "id": "cv_marvin_v1", "version": "1.0.0", "calibration": { ... } },
364	    { "id": "adc_fretboard", "version": "1.0.0", "thresholds": { ... } }
365	  ],
366	  "timing": { "chord_window_ms": 20, "strum_delay_ms": 220, "fret_early_ms": 50, "strum_pulse_ms": 50 },
367	  "ended_utc": null
368	}
369	```
370	
371	Written at session start; `ended_utc` is patched on a clean stop.
372	
373	#### 4.6.6 On-device buffering
374	
375	A FreeRTOS task (`record_task`) owns SD writes. State / command / ADC streams are small and write through directly. Keyframes are larger — a single keyframe at 1.04 MB cannot block the video pipeline, so the record task receives a **frame buffer pointer** (the same DDR buffer the ISC writes into; refcounted by the video task) and writes from DDR while the next frame is being captured into another buffer. We need ≥ 3 capture frame buffers (one capturing, one displaying, one being recorded) when recording is active; today the video task already has multiple frames pre-allocated — exact count is verified during implementation.
376	
377	If the SD write FIFO falls behind (rare; only a sustained-throughput problem), the recorder drops keyframes (logs a `RECORD_DROP` event into `state.bin`'s metadata channel) but **never** drops detector-state records.
378	
379	#### 4.6.7 Off-board detectors recording independently
380	
381	When a future Edge-AI detection unit is brought online, it can:
382	
383	- Subscribe to marvin's `frame_epoch` over a chosen link (UART/Ethernet/etc.).
384	- Record its own observations (e.g. its own sensor data + its own detector output) in its own format, *keyed by marvin's `frame_epoch`*.
385	- Be aligned post-hoc against marvin's reference recording during training.
386	
387	The spec does not constrain how off-board detectors store their data — only the sync contract (`frame_epoch` timeline) is canonical.
388	
389	#### 4.6.8 On-demand full-frame snapshot (USB CDC) ✅
390	
391	Independent of the SD recording path above (M4, not started), marvin can export a single full-resolution frame on demand over the existing perf-log USB CDC link. The host sends `PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT`; the perf-drain task copies the current frame once into a staging buffer and streams it back as a top-to-bottom run of full-width `PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT` band records (each ≤ `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES`), all sharing one `frame_epoch`, the last flagged `PERF_STRIP_FLAG_LAST`. Bands are written straight to the sink (bypassing the small strip pool) and paced by the wire; emit is not gated by the STRIP type mask. `marvin-perf snapshot` reassembles and saves the frame (`.bgr` + sidecar `.json`, plus `.png` via Pillow). This is the offline-study on-ramp for the game-state work (§4.8) — no in-runtime role.
392	
393	### 4.7 System services 🚧
394	
395	Cross-cutting services not owned by any one subsystem:
396	
397	- **Logging** ✅ severity-filtered printf shim (commit `a79042f`).
398	- **Time** ✅ TC0 / SYS_TIME for OSAL.
399	- **Config persistence** 🚧 calibration values, mode toggles, last-used recording stride. Storage TBD (a config file on SD vs internal flash).
400	- **Watchdog** 🚧 not yet enabled.
401	- **OTA** ⚪ out of scope for now.
402	
403	### 4.8 Game-state awareness & control 🚧
404	
405	Note on numbering: this subsystem is logically a peer of §4.2–§4.6 (a video-frame consumer that emits typed events plus a controller that issues actuator commands). It lives at §4.8 only to avoid renumbering existing sections referenced from the journal and milestones.
406	
407	#### 4.8.1 Role
408	
409	Two related capabilities, both grounded in CV on the captured video stream:
410	
411	1. **Game-state observer.** Watch the screen; recognize what context the game is currently in — main menu, song-select, difficulty-select, in-game (gameplay), pause, score summary, etc. Surface that as typed events that the operator UI can render and the orchestrator below can act on.
412	2. **Game controller.** Expose high-level verbs ("start a single-player playthrough of song X on Hard", "go to the main menu", "select Practice mode"). Translate each verb into a sequence of fret/strum commands using the recognized current state and a known menu graph, monitor the screen for the expected state transitions, retry or back out on mismatch.
413	
414	This is *not* the gameplay note-detection path (§4.2). cv_marvin_v1 plays notes during gameplay; the game-state module decides *what to play* at the session level (which song, which difficulty, which mode) and gets us there from any starting screen.
415	
416	Recognition is bootstrapped offline: the on-demand snapshot path (§4.6.8) collects a corpus of real GH3 screens, detection algorithms are prototyped host-side in Python (`tools/gameplay/`) against that corpus, and only the proven GH3-specific logic is ported into the firmware `gameplay_engine` module. Per Q10, the approach favors fixed-region/color/glyph matching over general CV — GH3's screens, fonts, and layouts are static.
417	
418	**M9 progress:** Phase 1 (screen-context classifier: main_menu / song_select / gameplay / pause / score) and Phase 2 (section-select and song-name readers) are prototyped and ported to firmware (`gameplay_engine.c`); the MPLAB build is confirmed. Phase 3 (number/score readers) is not yet started. The firmware module is pending hardware validation.
419	
420	#### 4.8.2 Module shape
421	
422	- Owns its own FreeRTOS task (`game_task`).
423	- Subscribes to the video frame queue via the same multi-subscriber API used by detectors (§4.2.4); it is a video-frame consumer, **not** a detector. Its events do not flow on `xDetectorStateQueue`.
424	- Emits typed events on a separate, narrow bus (`xGameStateQueue`) — current_state changes, ambiguity warnings, error states.
425	- Orchestrator state for high-level verbs (current goal, expected next state, retry counter) lives inside `game_task`.
426	- Issues control commands by writing fret/strum bitmasks into the same fretboard-link path used by gameplay. Whether this routes through the timing pipeline (§4.4) or bypasses it is open Q11.
427	
428	#### 4.8.3 Game catalog & menu metadata
429	
430	The recognizer and the navigator both depend on per-game data:
431	
432	- **Recognizer templates.** Per-state visual signatures used by the CV recognizer — could be small reference images (template matching), color histograms, or text regions for OCR. Format chosen with the recognizer algorithm (open Q10).
433	- **Menu graph.** Nodes = recognized game states; edges = button sequences that move between them (e.g., "main_menu → song_select" = `[STRUM_DOWN, STRUM_DOWN, GREEN]`). Used by the navigator to plan a verb.
434	- **Song catalog.** Per-supported-game list of songs with the menu coordinates needed to select each one (which difficulty submenu, ordinal position in the list, etc.). Possibly augmented with metadata (BPM, length, expected difficulty score) for UI display and for reference-data labeling.
435	
436	Storage: compile-time tables for the per-game graph + a JSON or similar on the SD card for songlists and any user-editable bits. Exact split deferred until first concrete game is added.
437	
438	Scope today: target is **one game** — Guitar Hero (Wii) — to validate the design. Adding a second game is a metadata addition (new template set + new menu graph + new song catalog), not a structural change.
439	
440	#### 4.8.4 Interaction with other subsystems
441	
442	- **Detection (§4.2):** independent. cv_marvin_v1 runs only when the game-state observer reports `gameplay`. Outside gameplay, cv_marvin_v1 may be disabled to free CPU.
443	- **Timing pipeline (§4.4):** during gameplay the timing pipeline drives the actuators from detector-state. Outside gameplay it's idle, and the game-state controller drives actuators directly. Coordination and arbitration between the two is open Q11.
444	- **Operator UI (§4.5):** consumes game-state events to display the current screen the game is on; offers verbs as buttons / song-list pickers.
445	- **Recording (§4.6):** game-state transitions are useful session metadata. Either annotated into `state.bin` as a side channel or a sibling file (`game_state.bin`). To be decided when the recorder lands.
446	- **Fretboard link (§4.3):** shared command path. The fretboard MCU does not know whether a press is "gameplay note" or "menu navigation" — they're the same wire bits.
447	
448	#### 4.8.5 Open questions surfaced here
449	
450	See §9 for tracking entries. In summary:
451	
452	- **Q10** — Recognizer algorithm: template matching vs simple OCR vs region/color heuristics vs a small CNN. Trade-off is robustness vs CPU cost vs metadata authoring effort.
453	- **Q11** — Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline. Default is "they don't run at the same time" (gameplay vs menu), but the boundary needs to be explicit.
454	
455	### 4.9 Operator command console ✅
456	
457	An **interactive text console** over **FLEXCOM2 USART (115 200 8N1, ring-buffer mode)** — marvin's `PA13` (FLEXCOM2_IO0, `CLI_TX`) / `PA14` (FLEXCOM2_IO1, `CLI_RX`) — deliberately on a separate channel from the DBGU log/printf chatter — log output stays on DBGU, console I/O stays on FLEXCOM2, so neither pollutes the other.
458	
459	- **Why not Harmony `SYS_CONSOLE`/`SYS_COMMAND`:** those are MCC-config-coupled and live in regenerated files (this board already carries ~10 re-apply patches against clobbered generated code). The console is instead a small in-tree module (`console/console.{h,c}`) in the same shape as `fretboard_link`/`perf_log`: it owns the USART plib directly, is fully statically allocated, and is kept out of MCC via `user.cmake`.
460	- **Library:** [embedded-cli](https://github.com/funbiscuit/embedded-cli) (vendored under `default/src/third_party/embedded-cli/`, MIT), used in static-allocation mode (a fixed `CLI_UINT` buffer → no `malloc`). Provides line editing, history, and tab-completion.
461	- **Mechanics:** one FreeRTOS task drains the FLEXCOM2 RX ring (woken by a 1-byte read-threshold notification, like `fretboard_rx_task`), feeds bytes to embedded-cli, and runs the dispatcher. Output is written byte-by-byte into the TX ring.
462	- **Commands (v0):** `status`, `detect <cv|adc> <on|off>`, `active <cv|adc>`, `timing <on|off>`, `manual <on|off>`, `fret <g|r|y|b|o> <0|1>`, `strum <down|up>` — dispatching into the existing `Detector_*`, `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled`, and `ManualControl_*` setters. The binding table is a plain static array; adding a command is one row. Maps onto the §6 operating-mode toggles. (`record`/`game_*` toggles and runtime timing-constant setters are deferred until those subsystems / setters exist.)
463	
464	---
465	
466	## 5. External interfaces 🚧
467	
468	To be expanded once §4.3 (fretboard wire protocol) is settled. Will document:
469	
470	- Marvin ↔ fretboard UART framing, byte-for-byte.
471	- Recording on-disk binary layouts (the `_t` structs from §4.2.3 and §4.6 in canonical form, including endianness).
472	- USB-CDC dev console framing (if any), Ethernet ref-data stream framing (if/when added).
473	
474	## 6. Operating modes 🚧
475	
476	Default model: independent toggles (matches `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md`'s detect/actuate split). Confirmed direction; concrete toggle list:
477	
478	| Toggle | Effect |
479	|---|---|
480	| `detect_enable` | CV + ADC detectors run; detector-state bus is active. |
481	| `marvin_timing_enable` | marvin's chord FIFO / strum scheduler runs. When off, fretboard runs its own pipeline (§4.4 fallback). |
482	| `actuate_enable` | Commands are actually sent to fretboard. When off, marvin computes commands but suppresses them (dry-run). |
483	| `record_enable` | Recording task writes to SD. |
484	| `game_observe_enable` | Game-state observer task runs; `xGameStateQueue` is active. |
485	| `game_control_enable` | Game-state controller may issue actuator commands for menu navigation / session setup. Suppressed during `gameplay` state when timing pipeline is driving. |
486	
487	A handful of named composite modes (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record) are presets over these toggles. Replay specifically requires loading a prior recording from SD and playing detector-state events back through the timing pipeline against the original keyframes — UI affordance for that comes later.
488	
489	## 7. Build & deploy 🚧
490	
491	To be filled. Topics: MCC-clobbered files (which paths are safe to edit by hand vs. regenerate), `user.cmake` boundaries, flashing workflow, sequence of MCC steps to reproduce the project.
492	
493	## 8. Phasing & milestones 🚧
494	
495	Proposed order; each is a buildable demo:
496	
497	1. **M1 — Reference detector v0** (§4.2). One CV detector running on captured frames, publishing `detector_state_t` to the bus. No actuation. Proves the bus and the detection task structure.
498	2. **M2 — Fretboard link** (§4.3). UART up; ADC stream ingested; `adc_fretboard` detector publishing onto the bus alongside `cv_marvin_v1`.
499	3. **M3 — Timing pipeline + actuation** (§4.4). Chord FIFO + strum scheduling; commands sent over UART; fretboard actuates. End-to-end play possible.
500	4. **M4 — Recording to SD** (§4.6). SDMMC + FAT mount; record task writes state/commands/ADC/keyframes during a session.
501	5. **M5 — Operator UI v0** (§4.5). Live view with overlays; mode toggles. UI framework decided here.
502	6. **M6 — Calibration UI** (§4.5). Per-fret ROI placement + threshold tuning on the device.
503	7. **M7 — Replay** (§6). Load a recording from SD, replay through the timing pipeline.
504	8. **M8 — Standalone-fretboard fallback** (§4.4). Marvin-disabled-pipeline mode validated.
505	9. **M9 — Game-state observer v0** (§4.8). 🚧 Phases 1+2 ported to firmware and MPLAB build confirmed (screen classifier + section-select/song readers); pending hardware test. Phase 3 (number/score readers) not yet started. Full milestone done when all contexts recognized and surfaced as `xGameStateQueue` events.
506	10. **M10 — Game-state control v0** (§4.8). Navigator/closed-loop algorithm complete in `tools/gameplay` prototype; firmware port not started. Done when high-level verbs ("start single-player song X") drive menu navigation through the same fretboard link.
507	
508	Live-stream Ethernet, Edge-AI integration, and config-on-flash are post-M8.

1	# marvin — Working Journal
2	
3	Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for marvin. Newest entries at the top. For *what marvin is* (purpose, subsystems, interfaces, milestones), read [`spec.md`](spec.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Current focus
8	
9	**T1S inter-node link — built and working (marvin ↔ guitar).** marvin is the PLCA **coordinator** (node 0) on a 10BASE-T1S bus (LAN8651 over FLEXCOM4 SPI); hand-authored stack in `default/src/net/t1s/`. It sends the actuator command over T1S to the `guitar` follower node (id 2), which actuates the Wii GPIOs (guitar G1+G2 proven). Followers announce presence via a heartbeat (ethertype `0x88B6`); the `t1s` and `nodes` console commands report link/credits/per-node presence. Transport is behind `MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT={UART,T1S}` (T1S default on the `t1s` branch). The `fretboard` node (id 1) firmware is now **written, T1S-only** (fretboard journal 2026-06-17): it streams its 17-byte frame to marvin **and** drives the `guitar` node directly — its on-device model infers the bitmask and sends it peer-to-peer to `02:..:02`. marvin's RX side needed no changes — `fretboard_link.c`'s T1S frame handler already parses the frame from node id 1 (`DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD`) and the node-table + heartbeat-presence demux already cover it. **Next (marvin side):** **active-source arbitration** — both marvin (timing pipeline) and the fretboard now address the guitar (`02:..:02`), so marvin needs active-detector/active-guitar selection to ensure exactly one source drives at a time (the fretboard's SW0 is an interim manual arm; until then, don't run marvin's timing pipeline to the guitar while the fretboard is armed). Then fretboard hardware bring-up. PoDL is design-direction only. Detail in [`../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md); decision log entry 2026-06-17.
10	
11	**Board port: SAM9X75 Curiosity → Curiosity Hybrid (in progress).** USB Host is gone on the Hybrid; the fretboard link was rewired from USB CDC host to a direct FLEXCOM2 USART on 2026-06-08 (see decision log + session log). Code-complete and syntax-checked; pending a full MPLAB build and on-hardware bring-up. Display/MIPI I²C (incl. TC358743 control) also moved off FLEXCOM6/PA24-PA25 to FLEXCOM8 TWI/PB4-PB5 during the port — `spec.md` §3.1/§3.2 reconciled on 2026-06-08. Dated 2026-05-01/05-20 journal entries and `journal-archive.md` keep their FLEXCOM6 references as historical record (true on the original Curiosity board).
12	
13	**M1 — Reference detector v0.** First CV detector running on captured frames, publishing `detector_state_t` records onto the detector-state bus. No actuation yet. See [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.2 for subsystem detail and §8 for the milestone progression.

SAM-BA's `writeboot` synthesizes this; a plain `nand write` does not, so headerless writes give RomBOOT-only (no boot). Fix: prepend the header with `binaries/make-pmecchead.sh` (wraps at91bootstrap `addpmecchead.py`) using the **real** chip params → word `0xc2605007`; *not* that script's SAM9X7 defaults (2048/64/4), which don't match this board. The previous comment ("fretboard side ignores baud over USB CDC") was wrong; only matters that the *application* on the PIC32 doesn't see the CDC line-coding fields, but the EDBG bridge in between very much does. `tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py` still hardcodes `ACTUATOR_BAUDRATE = 115200` for the same physical link — flagged as a follow-up; out of scope for this commit (different subproject). |
48	| 2026-06-01 | Perf-log v3 schema bump: add `DETECTOR_CONFIG` (cv_marvin_v1 sample coords/thresholds/color filters), `ACTUATOR` (intended/asserted masks + `producer_id` + ack timing), extend `TIMING` to a per-frame snapshot (chord window mask, note/strum queue head + deadlines, release timers, frets_active), and add `PERF_TASK_IDLE` + `PERF_TASK_OTHER` pseudo-slots so per-window CPU% adds to 100%. | Wire's job pivots from "prove bytes survived and the pipeline isn't dropping" (v1/v2 integrity story, complete) to "show the host what the detection algorithm and actuator are thinking" (tuning visibility). Bundling four additions into one schema cut avoids three rounds of firmware/host sync. Granular MCC-task breakdown deferred — not needed at this time. Causal-trace `TIMING_EVENT`, ISR latency histograms, Cortex-A5 PMU counters, free-heap reporting also out of scope this round. Plan details in 2026-06-01 session log entry. |
49	| 2026-05-29 | Patch the UDPHS device driver to arm DMA for queued IRPs in completion ISRs. New helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` called after queue advance in `Tasks_ISR_DMA` and the ZLP-completion path. Logged as patch #9. | Stock Harmony USB v3.16.0 driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch — IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in the linked list but never get armed for transmission. Without this, `queueSizeWrite > 1` accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch — we'd accept three perf-log strips, transmit one, the other two stranded forever. The IRP-queue infrastructure is *already there* in the driver, the missing piece is the post-completion arm. Fix is additive (new helper, two new call sites, no refactor of existing IRPSubmit body), making it easy to find/maintain after MCC regen. Future Harmony versions may obviate this if upstream wires it up. |
50	| 2026-05-29 | Strip queue uses 1-byte slot indices into a static `s_strip_pool[depth+2]` instead of pass-by-value `perf_rec_strip_t` items. | FreeRTOS queues are pass-by-value: every `xQueueSend`/`xQueueReceive` does `memcpy(slot, src, item_size)` inside a critical section (interrupts disabled). At `sizeof(perf_rec_strip_t) = 23-61 KB`, that was 38-100 µs of interrupts-off time per queue op × ~240 ops/s. Pool-and-index pattern moves the pixel data into a static pool indexed by 1-byte handles; queue ops drop to 1 µs critical sections. Same total BSS footprint (eliminates the producer's `static r;` and drain's `static s_strip_drain;` — pool size matches old "queue + 2 staging" footprint). Pool size `depth + 2` covers "1 slot in producer's hand + 1 in drain's hand" while preserving drop-on-full semantics. |

```text
1	# marvin HDMI → BGR888 Capture Pipeline
2	
3	Authoritative configuration reference for the 720p60 HDMI capture path on SAM9X75. Every stage, every register bit that matters, with datasheet citations. When something breaks, start here before grepping code.
4	
5	**Status:** working as of 2026-05-02. Validated at **1280×720p60** and **720×480p60**, native BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel) in DDR, no CPU post-processing. The pipeline is resolution-agnostic — PFE crop, DMA size, and framebuffer offsets all scale from the TC358743-detected `{width, height}` automatically.
6	
7	Datasheet references are to **SAM9X7 Series DS60001813** (sections 48 = MIPI CSI / D-PHY, 49 = CSI2DC, 50 = ISC). TC358743 refs are to the Toshiba datasheet + mainline Linux `drivers/media/i2c/tc358743.c`.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Pipeline overview
12	
13	```
14	HDMI source (Pi 720p60 RGB)
15	        │
16	        ▼
17	TC358743 HDMI-to-CSI-2 bridge
18	  DT=0x24 RGB888, 2 lanes, 972 Mbps/lane, continuous-clock mode
19	        │
20	        ▼                          <── MIPI CSI-2 D-PHY
21	SAM9X75 DWC D-PHY RX Gen3
22	  HSFREQRANGE=0x0A (950–1000 Mbps band)
23	        │
24	        ▼                          <── 40-bit isc_data bus
25	CSI2DC (Demultiplexer Controller)
26	  VPCFGR: DT=0x24, VC=0, PA=0, RMS=1  (byte-stream mode)
27	  → 4 BGR pixels packed into 12 bytes per CSI-2 RMS spec (Table 49.27)
28	        │
29	        ▼                          <── byte-stream on vp_data bus
30	ISC — Parallel Front End (PFE)
31	  PFE_CFG0: MIPI=1, BPS=FORTY, MODE=PROGRESSIVE, CONT=1, COLEN=1, ROWEN=1
32	  PFE_CFG1: COLMIN=0, COLMAX=(W×3/4)-1   (e.g. 959 at 1280px)
33	  PFE_CFG2: ROWMIN=0, ROWMAX=H-1   (719)
34	        │
35	        ▼                          <── sub420_data[39:0]
36	ISC — Rounding/Limiting/Packing (RLP)
37	  RLP_CFG: MODE=BYPASS (15)
38	  → rlp_data[31:0] = sub420_data[31:0] (pass-through)
39	        │
40	        ▼                          <── rlp_data[31:0]
41	ISC — DMA Host
42	  DCFG: IMODE=PACKED32, YMBSIZE=BEATS32, CMBSIZE=BEATS32
43	  → stores 32-bit words to DDR; RMS=1 byte-stream → dense BGR888
44	        │
45	        ▼
46	DDR3 framebuffer  (1280 × 720 × 3 = 2,764,800 B/frame)
47	  B G R  B G R  B G R  ...  (dense, no padding byte)
48	```
49	
50	---
51	
52	## 2. Stage-by-stage configuration
53	
54	### 2.1 HDMI source
55	
56	- 1280×720p @ 60 Hz, RGB (not YCbCr), progressive.
57	- Any stable DVI/HDMI source works. Raspberry Pi with `/boot/firmware/config.txt` forced to `hdmi_group=1 hdmi_mode=4 hdmi_force_hotplug=1 hdmi_drive=2` is the known-good reference.
58	- Pixel rate: 74.25 MHz (standard CEA-861 VIC 4 / 720p60).
59	
60	Full-range vs limited-range is sender-controlled. TC358743's AVI InfoFrame carries whatever the source advertises; currently Pi sends limited-range, so peak values in DDR are `0xFE` not `0xFF`. EDID colorimetry overrides are a separate future task.
61	
62	### 2.2 TC358743 HDMI-to-CSI-2 bridge
63	
64	Driver: `firmware/marvin/default/src/tc358743.c`. Register values derived from mainline Linux `tc358743.c`.
65	
66	| Register | Value | Meaning |
67	|---|---|---|
68	| `PLLCTL` PRD=4, FBD=144 | PLL out = 972 MHz | `hsck = (27 MHz / PRD) × FBD` |
69	| `CSI_CONFW` lanes | 2 | 2 data lanes × 972 Mbps = 1.944 Gbps total (plenty for 720p60 RGB888's ~1.33 Gbps) |
70	| `CONFCTL` | 0x0007 | PCLK divider off, 3-byte pixel pack, no audio |
71	| `FIFOCTL` | 0x0176 | FIFO level 374 (kernel hardcodes at all rates) |
72	| `VI_MODE` | 0xE6 | RGB888 input, 16-bit HDMI RX side |
73	| `VI_REP`  | 0x00 | **No pixel replication / doubling** (critical — was 0x80 in earlier 480p test and caused 16-row phase drift) |
74	| `VOUT_SET2` / `VOUT_SET3` | 0x01 / 0x08 | Output color format / range handling |
75	| CSI-2 DT | 0x24 | RGB888 per CSI-2 spec |
76	
77	D-PHY timing (for 972 Mbps):
78	```
79	LINEINITCNT  = 0x1B58
80	LPTXTIMECNT  = 0x0007
81	TCLK_HEADER  = 0x2806    TCLK_TRAIL  = 0x0000    TCLK_POST = 0x0008
82	THS_HEADER   = 0x0806    THS_TRAIL   = 0x0005
83	TWAKEUP      = 0x4268    HSTXVREGCNT = 0x0000
84	```
85	
86	Operating mode: **continuous clock** (`TXOPTIONCNTRL = CONTCLKMODE`). This is the required-match with the SAM9X75 RX side — if RX expects gated but TX sends continuous (or vice versa), `CSI2DC.GSR.ARSTIP` hangs permanently.
87	
88	### 2.3 SAM9X75 MIPI CSI-2 D-PHY RX
89	
90	Driver: `firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/csi/` (MCC-generated, slightly tweaked).
91	
92	Key setting — **the one parameter that took us the longest to get right**:
93	
94	```c
95	// isc_capture.c:25
96	#define ISC_CAP_CSI_BITRATE  0x0Au
97	```
98	
99	This is the `HSFREQRANGE` DWC D-PHY test-mode value. SAM9X75 is **DWC Gen3** (verified from Linux DT: `snps,dw-dphy-rx` with `snps,phy_type=<0>`). The Gen3 table entry for the 950–1000 Mbps band is `0x0A`.
100	
101	- **Wrong** (used during earlier debug): `0x1A` — that's a Gen2 value. At 972 Mbps Gen2 bands diverge from Gen3, symptom is persistent `PHY_FATAL.SOT_SYNC_ERR = 0x3`.
102	- **Correct** for 972 Mbps Gen3: `0x0A`.
103	- Changes with bitrate. If bitrate moves, look up Gen3 table (DesignWare MIPI D-PHY RX Gen3 Databook), don't copy values from other SoC examples.
104	
105	Other CSI settings:
106	- `CSI_NUM_LANES = 2` (matches TC358743).
107	- `csiObj->csiFps = 60u` (informational; drives some timing in the driver).
108	
109	### 2.4 CSI2DC — the RMS=1 lever
110	
111	**This is the key decision that enables in-pipeline BGR888 packed.** DS60001813 §49.6.54:
112	
113	| VPCFGR Field | Value | Reason |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| DT (bits 5:0) | 0x24 | RGB888 (matches TC358743 emission) |
116	| VC (bits 7:6) | 0 | Virtual channel 0 |
117	| PA (bit 14) | **0** | LSB-aligned. PA=1 is for 10/12-bit Bayer sensors being packed onto ISC's 12-bit internal bus. Irrelevant for MIPI RGB888 bypass. |
118	| **RMS (bit 13)** | **1** | **Critical.** See below. |
119	| RGB36MAP (bit 15) | 0 | Use Table 49.27 pixel mapping |
120	
121	`RMS` (Recommended Memory Storage) per datasheet:
122	
123	- `RMS=0` — "CSI2DC outputs 1 pixel per component per clock cycle, compliant with the ISC processing engine." → Table 49.25: `demux_data[39:24]=0`, `[23:16]=R`, `[15:8]=G`, `[7:0]=B`. One pixel per 40-bit VP word — gives BGRX32 (4 B/pixel, 25% extra DDR bandwidth, X byte always 0x00).
124	- `RMS=1` — "CSI2DC generates a byte stream compliant with the CSI-2 specification memory format." → Table 49.27: 4 BGR pixels packed into 12 bytes. Results in **dense 3 B/pixel BGR888** — 25% less DDR bandwidth, and XLCDC HEO reads natively in `RGB_888_PACKED` mode.
125	
126	**MCC's default omits RMS=1.** We add it (re-apply patch #3):
127	
128	```c
129	// firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/csi2dc/plib_csi2dc.c
130	void CSI2DC_Configure_VideoPipe(uint32_t dt, uint32_t vc, uint32_t align_isc) {
131	    CSI2DC_REGS->CSI2DC_VPCFGR = CSI2DC_VPCFGR_DT(dt)
132	                               | CSI2DC_VPCFGR_VC(vc)
133	                               | (align_isc ? CSI2DC_VPCFGR_PA_1 : 0)
134	                               | CSI2DC_VPCFGR_RMS_1;  /* PATCH #3: byte-stream mode */
135	}
136	```
137	
138	Other CSI2DC config:
139	- `GCFGR.MIPIFRN = 0` (free-running, matches TC358743's continuous-clock mode). MCC default is gated (`MIPIFRN=1`); mismatch leaves `CSI2DC.GSR.ARSTIP` stuck on reset. Override via `csi2dcObj->enableMIPIFreeRun = true;` in `isc_capture.c`.
140	- `VPER = 1` (video pipe enabled).
141	
142	### 2.5 ISC — Parallel Front End (PFE)
143	
144	DS60001813 §50.6.6, §50.7.4–50.7.6.
145	
146	Key settings configured by `DRV_ISC_Configure()`:
147	
148	| PFE_CFG0 field | Value | Why |
149	|---|---|---|
150	| REP | 0 | N/A for BPS=FORTY |
151	| BPS (30:28) | 5 = FORTY | "40-bit input (used for MIPI formats up to forty bits per pixel)." Matches CSI2DC's 40-bit VP bus. |
152	| MIPI (bit 14) | 1 | Input from MIPI interface |
153	| GATED (bit 8) | 0 | Free-running clock |
154	| CCIR656 (bit 9) | 0 | Not embedded-sync — using MIPI |
155	| CONT (bit 7) | 1 | Continuous acquisition (vs single shot) |
156	| MODE (6:4) | 0 = PROGRESSIVE | Source is progressive |
157	| VPOL / HPOL | 0 | Active-high sync (standard) |
158	
159	**Two bits that MCC leaves OFF but we must set:**
160	
161	| PFE_CFG0 field | Value | Why MCC misses it |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| **COLEN (bit 12)** | **1** | Enables the column crop window |
164	| **ROWEN (bit 13)** | **1** | Enables the row crop window |
165	
166	MCC's `ISC_PFE_Crop_Area()` function is defined in `plib_isc.c` but **never called**. Without COLEN+ROWEN and valid COLMAX/ROWMAX, the PFE expects a 1×1 frame and fires HDTO (Horizontal Detection Timeout) on the first real line. The Linux `mchp-isc` driver sets both bits; we match that.
167	
168	We program these directly after `DRV_ISC_Configure()`. With RMS=1, COLMAX is in ISC sample units (32-bit byte-stream words), so the formula is `(width × 3 / 4) - 1`:
169	
170	```c
171	// isc_capture.c
172	ISC_REGS->ISC_PFE_CFG1 = ISC_PFE_CFG1_COLMIN(0u)
173	                       | ISC_PFE_CFG1_COLMAX((width * 3u / 4u) - 1u);  // 959 at 1280px
174	ISC_REGS->ISC_PFE_CFG2 = ISC_PFE_CFG2_ROWMIN(0u)
175	                       | ISC_PFE_CFG2_ROWMAX((uint32_t)height - 1u);   // 719 at 720p
176	ISC_REGS->ISC_PFE_CFG0 |= ISC_PFE_CFG0_COLEN_1 | ISC_PFE_CFG0_ROWEN_1;
177	```
178	
179	With RMS=1, COLMAX is in **byte-stream word units** (4 bytes per ISC sample), so COLMAX = `(W × 3) / 4 - 1`. Under the previous RMS=0 path, COLMAX was in pixel units (`W - 1`).
180	
181	### 2.6 ISC — Rounding, Limiting, Packing (RLP)
182	
183	DS60001813 §50.6.19, §50.7.67.
184	
185	| RLP_CFG field | Value | Reason |
186	|---|---|---|
187	| **MODE (3:0)** | **15 = BYPASS** | "32-bit input is sampled and written to the rlp output port. Select this mode for MIPI RMS mode." Passes `sub420_data[31:0]` through unchanged. With our RMS=0 input that's `0x00RRGGBB`. |
188	| ALPHA (15:8) | — | Ignored in BYPASS mode (only used by ARGB444/ARGB555/ARGB32 modes) |
189	| YMODE / LSH / REP | 0 | Not applicable to BYPASS |
190	
191	**Why not ARGB32 RLP (Mode 10)?** Per §50.6.19 Table row for RGB32/ARGB32:
192	```
193	rlp_data[31:24] = A = ALPHA[7:0]       (register)
194	rlp_data[23:16] = R = sub420_data[29:22]
195	rlp_data[15:8]  = G = sub420_data[19:12]
196	rlp_data[7:0]   = B = sub420_data[9:2]
197	```
198	
199	These bit positions are the output format of the ISC **CSC module** (Color Space Conversion, §50.6.15), not raw MIPI RGB888. On our bypass path, R/G/B sit at `[23:16]/[15:8]/[7:0]` — a 6/4/2-bit shift off what ARGB32 RLP wants. Attempting it yields mangled 3-shifted-copies-of-garbage per 12 bytes. **ARGB32 RLP is structurally unusable for MIPI RGB888 bypass;** it would require enabling the full demosaic pipeline (for Bayer sources) or CSC (for YCbCr).
200	
201	Consequence: we cannot get `alpha = 0xFF` in-pipeline for free. We get `alpha = 0x00` because CSI2DC zeros the upper 16 bits of each 40-bit VP word. If `0xFF` alpha matters, a one-shot CPU pass to set `buf[3::4] = 0xFF` does it cheaply, or stamp 0xFF into the framebuffer once at init (DMA writes never touch byte 3 if pixel stride matches — need to verify that assumption before relying on it).
202	
203	**Driver hint:** `iscObj->rlpMode = ISC_RLP_CFG_MODE_BYPASS` (value 15 in the MCC enum). `drv_isc.c` writes this into RLP_CFG during `DRV_ISC_Configure`.
204	
205	### 2.7 ISC — DMA Host
206	
207	DS60001813 §50.6.20, §50.7.70.
208	
209	| DCFG field | Value | Reason |
210	|---|---|---|
211	| **IMODE (2:0)** | **2 = PACKED32** | "32 bits, single channel packed." Stores each `rlp_data[31:0]` as 4 contiguous bytes in memory. With RMS=1 byte-stream, this writes dense BGR888 — every 3rd byte is the start of the next pixel, no padding. |
212	| YMBSIZE (6:4) | 4 = BEATS32 | 32-beat AXI burst (sama7g5 / SAM9X7 — MCC's PACKED8 default is BEATS8 which is the sama5d2 value, undersized for this SoC). |
213	| CMBSIZE (10:8) | 4 = BEATS32 | Same rationale as YMBSIZE. |
214	| ARQOS / AWQOS | 0 | Dynamic QoS based on FIFO level (recommended default) |
215	
216	MCC's `DRV_ISC_Configure` sets PACKED8 + BEATS8 if `iscObj->layout = ISC_LAYOUT_PACKED8`. We override after `DRV_ISC_Configure`:
217	
218	```c
219	// isc_capture.c:219-221
220	ISC_REGS->ISC_DCFG = ISC_DCFG_IMODE_PACKED32
221	                   | ISC_DCFG_YMBSIZE_BEATS32
222	                   | ISC_DCFG_CMBSIZE_BEATS32;
223	```
224	
225	The write is safe because nothing in MCC writes DCFG again after this point (the redundant-call to `DRV_ISC_Configure_DMA` was removed). `DRV_ISC_Configure` already calls it internally at `drv_isc.c:381` — don't add a second call.
226	
227	**Descriptor view:** `DCTRL.DVIEW = 0` (PACKED / single channel). `DAD0` holds the current buffer base address. `DST0` = 0 (contiguous frame, no row stride gap).
228	
229	### 2.8 Framebuffer layout in DDR
230	
231	```c
232	// isc_capture.c
233	#define ISC_CAP_MAX_W        1280u
234	#define ISC_CAP_MAX_H        720u
235	#define ISC_CAP_BPP          3u      /* BGR888 packed */
236	#define ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS  4u
237	
238	static __attribute__((__section__(".region_nocache")))
239	       __attribute__((__aligned__(32)))
240	       uint8_t g_framebuffer[ISC_CAP_MAX_W * ISC_CAP_MAX_H * ISC_CAP_BPP * ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS];
241	```
242	
243	- Pool size: 1280×720×3×4 = ~11 MB, in the **uncached** DDR region (`.region_nocache`).
244	- Uncached so CPU vision consumers (cv_marvin_v1) see DMA-fresh bytes without D-cache invalidation.
245	- 32-byte aligned (cache line boundary).
246	- At 480p: only 720×480×3×4 = ~4.1 MB actually used.
247	- 4-deep ring gives slow consumers up to ~50 ms read window before lapping.
248	
249	Pixel access pattern (0-indexed, little-endian):
250	
251	```c
252	uint8_t *px = &g_framebuffer[(y * W + x) * 4];
253	uint8_t B = px[0];
254	uint8_t G = px[1];
255	uint8_t R = px[2];
256	// px[3] = 0x00 (X / unused)
257	```
258	
259	As a 32-bit word: `*(uint32_t*)px == 0x00RRGGBB` (native little-endian).
260	
261	### Sizing strategy
262	
263	The buffer pool is statically allocated for the **maximum supported resolution** (`ISC_CAP_MAX_W × ISC_CAP_MAX_H × ISC_CAP_BPP × ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS` = 1920 × 1080 × 4 × 2 = 15.8 MB), reserved once at link time in `.region_cache_aligned`. Per-capture the ISC DMA descriptor is programmed for only `width × height × 4` bytes; the rest of the pool sits idle.
264	
265	| Resolution | In use / frame | 2-buffer total | Idle |
266	|---|---|---|---|
267	| 480p60 | 1.32 MB | 2.64 MB | 13.2 MB |
268	| 720p60 | 3.69 MB | 7.37 MB | 8.4 MB |
269	| 1080p60 | 7.90 MB | 15.8 MB | 0 |
270	
271	Trade-off: idle DDR at low resolutions (trivial on this 256 MB platform) in exchange for zero reallocation on source-resolution change — buffer base pointers stay constant, the consumer never needs to re-bind. `ISC_Capture_Configure` rejects any `width > MAX_W || height > MAX_H` so the guarantee is enforced.
272	
273	---
274	
275	## 3. Verified output — color sweep
276	
277	Pi source, 720p60 RGB limited-range (so peak = 0xFE). Probe reports memory at representative points across the frame:
278	
279	| Source color | Memory (`b0 b1 b2 b3`) | Decode |
280	|---|---|---|
281	| Red   | `00 00 FE 00` | B=0, G=0, R=0xFE, X=0 |
282	| Green | `00 FE 00 00` | B=0, G=0xFE, R=0, X=0 |
283	| Blue  | `FE 00 00 00` | B=0xFE, G=0, R=0, X=0 |
284	| White | `FE FE FE 00` | B=G=R=0xFE, X=0 |
285	| Black | `00 00 00 00` | — |
286	
287	All five match expectation across the full 1280×720 extent (rows 0..719 completely written, no cliff). Framerate sustained at 70 fps probe-window average (≈60 fps real + diagnostic ticks).
288	
289	---
290	
291	## 4. Where each override lives in code
292	
293	| Stage | File | Line | Change |
294	|---|---|---|---|
295	| TC358743 D-PHY timing | `default/src/tc358743.c` | 25–33 | 972 Mbps timing constants (kernel-derived) |
296	| TC358743 PLL | `default/src/tc358743.c` | 14–20 | `PLL_PRD=4`, `PLL_FBD=144` |
297	| CSI HSFREQRANGE | `default/src/isc_capture.c` | 23 | `0x0A` for DWC Gen3 @ 972 Mbps |
298	| CSI bitrate override | `default/src/isc_capture.c` | 83 | `csiObj->csiBitRate = ISC_CAP_CSI_BITRATE` (MCC default is `0x16`) |
299	| CSI2DC RMS=0 | `default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/csi2dc/plib_csi2dc.c` | 71–78 | dropped `CSI2DC_VPCFGR_RMS_1` from VPCFGR write |
300	| CSI2DC free-run | `default/src/isc_capture.c` | 88 | `enableMIPIFreeRun = true` |
301	| ISC PFE crop | `default/src/isc_capture.c` | 195–202 | direct `PFE_CFG1/2` + `COLEN`/`ROWEN` writes |
302	| ISC DMA config | `default/src/isc_capture.c` | 209–211 | direct `DCFG` write (PACKED32 + BEATS32×2) |
303	| Framebuffer BPP | `default/src/isc_capture.c` | 17 | `ISC_CAP_BPP = 4` |
304	
305	---
306	
307	## 5. Debug / diagnostics
308	
309	Runtime log is intentionally quiet — initialization, format detection, and a one-shot pre-start register snapshot only. No periodic dump.
310	
311	What lands on the DBGU during normal operation:
312	
313	1. **TC358743 init + lock sequence** — I2C presence, init, SYS_STATUS transitions as HDMI negotiates, final `detected WxH @ FPS, RGB ...` with raster dimensions.
314	2. **`ISC_Capture: configured WxH BGRX32 (N bytes/frame)`** — called by `app_coordinate_capture` when TC358743 reports a locked format.
315	3. **`ISC_Capture diag (pre-start):` block** — one-shot register snapshot printed from `diag_dump_rx()` right before `DRV_ISC_Start_Capture`. Contains CSI / CSI2DC / ISC state at the moment capture is armed. When diagnosing new sources or regressions, this is the first place to look.
316	4. **`ISC_Capture: capture started`** — green light. Quiet from here.
317	5. **TC358743 format-change events** — if the source switches resolution mid-run, the watcher prints a new detection line and the capture module re-configures.
318	
319	If deeper inspection is needed (byte-level probes, phase scanners, content bounding box), resurrect `ISC_Capture_ProbeFrame()` from git history (commit `29a21bf` has the last full version) and wire it into a temporary 1-Hz tick.
320	
321	---
322	
323	## 6. Known carry-forwards
324	
325	- **`INTSR.HDTO` always set** after capture start — informational-only residual, not a stop signal. Also present under working RMS=1 config. Safe to ignore.
326	- **DDONE interrupt unreliable** — `iscObj->frameIndex` advances rarely or not at all; `g_frame_count` (incremented from the frame-done callback, driven by VD) counts correctly. DMA itself works (buffers update on schedule). Investigate before building consumer logic that relies on DDONE firing per frame.
327	- **Pixel range 0x00–0xFE** because TC358743 passes through source's limited-range signaling. EDID overrides or TC358743 colorimetry registers can force full-range; deferred until display stage forces the issue.
328	- **Alpha channel = 0x00** — not 0xFF. Acceptable for display framebuffers that ignore alpha; requires CPU fix-up if alpha is semantic.
329	
330	---
331	
332	## 7. Datasheet-anchored reasoning for ARGB/RGBA aspirations
333	
334	If someone revisits this and asks "can we get ARGB32 directly in-pipeline?":
335	
336	1. **ARGB32 RLP mode** requires upstream data at `sub420_data[29:22]/[19:12]/[9:2]`. That's the CSC output format (§50.6.15). CSC is a module for converting to/from YCbCr — it's not a pass-through. Routing RGB888 through CSC would work only if CSC has an identity-RGB mode, which per §50.6.15 it doesn't (the CSC input is YCbCr by design).
337	2. **Demosaic pipeline** (WB → CFA → CC → GAM → …) expects 10/12-bit Bayer mosaic input, not 24-bit RGB.
338	3. **CSI2DC has no alpha-insertion register** — only RMS mode and the RGB36MAP packing variant. Neither affects the upper byte.
339	
340	Therefore the cleanest path to ARGB32 is:
341	- **Software post-pass:** single `memset` of byte 3 at framebuffer init (if DMA stride matches) or a per-frame byte-smearing pass (expensive).
342	- **GFX2D blit:** use the 2D graphics engine to copy BGRX32 → ARGB32 with alpha fill. Zero CPU cost if the engine supports it.
343	- **Display IP native BGRX support:** SAM9X75 LCDC supports multiple BGRX/ARGB layouts — pick one that doesn't care about alpha. Probably the right answer.
344
```

1	# marvin — System Specification
2	
3	> **Read this first** for any non-trivial marvin task. The journal ([`journal.md`](journal.md)) is the running diary of decisions and work-in-progress; this spec is the durable description of *what marvin is*. When the two disagree, fix the spec.
4	
5	**Status:** in-progress draft. Sections that are settled are marked ✅; sections that depend on open architectural questions are marked 🚧 and link to the relevant entries in §9.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Purpose & scope
10	
11	### 1.1 What marvin is
12	
13	marvin is the firmware running on a **SAM9X75 Curiosity** board. Its job, in the guitar-playing-robot system, is to:
14	
15	1. Capture live HDMI video of a Guitar Hero / Rock Band game from a Nintendo Wii.
16	2. Run computer-vision note detection on the captured frames.
17	3. Decide *what* to play and *when* (chord grouping, fret-early timing, strum scheduling).
18	4. Send the corresponding fret/strum commands to the actuator controller (the **fretboard** MCU).
19	5. Provide an on-device operator UI (10.1″ LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch) for live view, calibration, mode selection, logs.
20	6. Produce **reference data** — annotated frames + detector state — for off-board use (training low-fidelity detectors, side-by-side detector comparison, replay).
21	7. **Observe game state from the screen** — recognize current menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score-summary contexts via CV, expose high-level control verbs ("start single-player playthrough of song X", "advance menu", "exit to main menu") that translate into fret/strum command sequences sent through the same fretboard link.
22	
23	In short: marvin is the runtime brain *and* the reference-detector data source for the project.
24	
25	### 1.2 What marvin is *not*
26	
27	- **Not the actuator.** Physical fret/strum GPIO drive lives on the fretboard MCU. marvin sends bitmask commands; fretboard converts them to button presses.
28	- **Not a sensor / detection-only device.** marvin owns timing and command emission. It is not a passive vision peripheral that some other host orchestrates.
29	- **Not a router for a PC.** The previous PC-based architecture (Elgato + OpenCV + USB to a Pi) is retired. marvin replaces the PC in the runtime path.
30	- **Not a generic camera platform.** The video source is a fixed HDMI signal from a game console. Suggestions like "just use a USB webcam" or "output to HDMI directly" miss the point.
31	
32	### 1.3 North-star one-paragraph summary
33	
34	A SAM9X75 captures Wii HDMI video at 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz over a TC358743 → MIPI CSI-2 → ISC path into DDR (BGR888 packed, 3 B/pixel). It runs reference-quality CV note detection on those frames, fuses with ADC-based detection ingested from a fretboard MCU over a FLEXCOM2 UART link, schedules chord/strum commands through a low-latency timing pipeline, sends commands back to the fretboard, drives an operator UI on a 10.1″ LVDS panel, and exports a compressed reference-data stream so that lighter-weight detectors (today: fretboard's phototransistors; future: an Edge AI MCU) can be trained against marvin's ground truth.
35	
36	### 1.4 What's done, what's next
37	
38	| Subsystem | Status |
39	|---|---|
40	| HDMI capture (TC358743 → CSI-2 → ISC → DDR, BGR888 packed) | ✅ working at 480p60 and 720p60. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md). |
41	| Display path (DDR → XLCDC HEO → LVDSC → panel) | ✅ working, pillarboxed/letterboxed, per-frame pointer swap. See [`display_path.md`](display_path.md). |
42	| FreeRTOS scheduler, video task, OSAL I²C | ✅ landed. |
43	| Lightweight log shim, FreeRTOS analytics, task priorities | ✅ done. |
44	| CV detection pipeline | 🚧 M1 complete: `cv_marvin_v1` running on captured frames, `detector_state_t` bus active. No actuation path through detector yet. §4.2. |
45	| Fretboard link (FLEXCOM2 USART) | ✅ working; gameplay tested over the original USB CDC host link. Link rewired to a direct FLEXCOM2 UART for the Curiosity Hybrid board (no host-capable USB port); pending on-hardware re-validation. §4.3. |
46	| Timing pipeline (chord FIFO, strum) | ✅ working; end-to-end gameplay tested on Expert and Easy. §4.4. |
47	| Operator UI (Legato) | 🚧 Manual-control surface (8 buttons, Legato Composer) done; full calibration/log UI not started. §4.5, open Q5. |
48	| Reference-data recording & export (SD) | 🚧 SD recording not started. Perf-log USB CDC export (separate dev-tooling path) complete at 2.77 MB/s. §4.6, open Q1/Q2. |
49	| System services (config, time, watchdog) | 🚧 Partial: logging, FreeRTOS analytics, static task priorities done; config persistence and watchdog not started. §4.7. |
50	| Game-state awareness & high-level game control | 🚧 M9 Phases 1+2 firmware-complete (screen classifier + section-select/song readers; MPLAB build confirmed, pending hardware test). M9 Phase 3 (number/score readers) and M10 (controller/navigator) not yet started in firmware. §4.8. |

123	### 2.2 Who owns what
124	
125	| Concern | Owner | Notes |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| HDMI capture into memory | marvin | TC358743 + CSI-2 + ISC; 720×480 / 1280×720 @ 60 Hz, BGR888 packed (3 B/pixel). |
128	| Reference-quality CV note detection | marvin | Ground truth; multiple algorithms may coexist on the bus. |
129	| ADC-based note detection | fretboard → marvin | fretboard scans 5 phototransistors @ 240 Hz, streams raw values; marvin runs the detector logic. |
130	| Detector-state fusion / arbitration | marvin | One canonical detector-state bus; the active source feeds the timing pipeline. |
131	| Chord-window FIFO + strum scheduling | marvin | Open Q4: stays on marvin (centralized) vs migrates to fretboard. Default: marvin. |
132	| Fret/strum GPIO output | fretboard | Open-drain pin drive only; receives a bitmask over UART. |
133	| Operator UI (live view, calibration, modes, logs) | marvin | 10.1″ LVDS + maxtouch. Open Q5: Legato vs custom. |
134	| Reference-data recording & export | marvin | Compressed/derived format; transport TBD (open Q1/Q2). |
135	| Game-state observation (menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score) | marvin | CV on captured frames; emits typed game-state events on its own bus. §4.8. |
136	| Game catalog + menu metadata (song list, menu graph, recognized icons) | marvin | Compile-time tables and/or SD-card JSON. Drives the recognizer and the navigator. §4.8. |
137	| High-level game control (e.g., "start single-player song X") | marvin | Translates verbs into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link as gameplay commands. §4.8. |
138	| Calibration / tuning UI authoring | dev PC (fret-tuner) | Optional; not required at runtime. Open Q7: long-term fate. |
139	| Training data ingest / replay analysis | dev PC | Off-band consumer of marvin's reference-data export. |
140	
141	### 2.3 Data flow at a glance
142	
143	1. **Frame ready** — ISC writes a BGR888 packed frame to DDR; the video task notifies subscribers.
144	2. **CV detect** — one or more CV detectors read the frame and emit detector-state events.
145	3. **ADC ingest** — a UART task receives raw ADC samples from the fretboard and runs an ADC detector that emits detector-state events on the same bus.
146	4. **Arbitrate** — the timing pipeline picks the active detector (or fuses), maintains the chord-accumulation window, and pushes finished chords onto its FIFO.
147	5. **Schedule** — the FIFO emits fret-assert and strum-pulse commands at the correct ticks.
148	6. **Send** — commands are encoded and transmitted to the fretboard over UART.
149	7. **Display** — the captured frame is composited with overlays (sensor crosshairs, detector outputs, chord state, latency markers) and shown on the LVDS panel.
150	8. **Record** (optional) — when recording is enabled, a derived/compressed reference-data record (frame epoch + detector state + raw ADC + emitted commands) is buffered and exported via the chosen transport.
151	
152	### 2.4 Latency budget (target, end-to-end)
153	
154	| Stage | Budget | Notes |
155	|---|---|---|
156	| HDMI source → DDR (capture) | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame @ 60 Hz; bounded by capture pipeline. |
157	| Detect on frame | ≤ 16.7 ms | One frame budget for CV; ADC path is separate and faster. |
158	| Timing pipeline → command emit | latency dominated by `STRUM_DELAY_MS` (≈ 200 ms) — intentional, not waste; compensates for sensor placement above strike line. |
159	| UART command → fretboard GPIO | ≤ 5 ms | Short fixed-format frame at ≥ 115 200 Bd. |
160	| Total user-visible latency | ≈ 200–250 ms | Tunable via `STRUM_DELAY_MS`, set per-game by calibration. |
161	
162	The dominant fixed delay (`STRUM_DELAY_MS`) exists by design — the camera sees notes before they reach the strike line. Capture + detect + UART jitter is what we actually budget against.
163	
164	---
