202	
203	## 4. Subsystems
204	
205	### 4.1 Video capture & display ✅
206	
207	Working end-to-end. See [`capture_pipeline.md`](capture_pipeline.md) and [`display_path.md`](display_path.md) for register-level detail. The video task (`video.c`, FreeRTOS) owns the capture pipeline and a frame queue that other tasks subscribe to. Display intent and capture intent are decoupled (commit `e28c497`); a software scaler can be inserted between capture and display when source ≠ panel native.
208	
209	**What this subsystem owns:**
210	- TC358743 init, source detection, EDID, format negotiation.
211	- ISC DMA configuration and frame buffer rotation in DDR.
212	- XLCDC overlay window placement (pillarbox/letterbox) for the active source.
213	- Frame-ready notification to subscribers (CV detect, recording, UI overlay).
214	
215	**What it doesn't own:**
216	- CV processing (§4.2).
217	- Recording / export (§4.6).
218	- UI widgets / chrome (§4.5) — only the pixel composition for the live-view layer.
219	
220	### 4.2 CV detection pipeline + detector-state bus 🚧
221	
222	#### 4.2.1 Role
223	
224	This is what makes marvin the *reference detector*. It runs computer-vision note detection on captured frames and publishes a structured detector-state record per frame onto a shared bus. Other detectors (fretboard ADC; future Edge-AI unit) publish onto the same bus. The timing pipeline (§4.4) consumes the bus.
225	
226	#### 4.2.2 Detector model
227	
228	A **detector** is anything that turns observation data into a `detector_state_t` event. marvin will host at least:
229	
230	- `cv_marvin_v1` — the reference vision detector. Reads RGB888-packed (3 B/pixel) frames from the video frame queue; emits one `detector_state_t` per frame.
231	- `adc_fretboard` — runs on top of raw ADC samples streamed from the fretboard MCU (§4.3); emits `detector_state_t` events at the fretboard's 240 Hz rate.
232	
233	Future detectors may include alternate CV algorithms running in parallel for comparison, or off-board detectors (Edge-AI MCU) feeding state in over UART/Ethernet.
234	
235	#### 4.2.3 detector_state record (canonical shape)
236	
237	```
238	typedef struct {
239	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     // master sync token (§4.6.4)
240	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    // monotonic, marvin-local
241	    uint8_t  detector_id;     // 0=cv_marvin_v1, 1=adc_fretboard, ...
242	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
243	    struct {
244	        uint8_t  pressed;     // 0/1 hard call
245	        uint16_t confidence;  // 0..65535, detector-defined
246	        uint16_t raw_value;   // detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc.
247	    } fret[5];                // FRET_GREEN..FRET_ORANGE
248	} detector_state_t;
249	```
250	
251	Fields are fixed-width, naturally aligned, little-endian — this is also the on-disk record layout for the state log (§4.6.5). `frame_epoch` is the master clock for cross-detector and cross-recording sync.
252	
253	#### 4.2.4 Bus mechanics
254	
255	- A single FreeRTOS queue (`xDetectorStateQueue`) carries `detector_state_t` records, one entry per detector emit.
256	- The timing pipeline task (§4.4) is the sole consumer.
257	- The recording task (§4.6) snoops the queue via a side-channel: each producer publishes simultaneously to the timing-pipeline queue and to a recording stream buffer. (Single producer→multiple consumers is implemented by tee'ing inside each detector, not by a broker; keeps queue semantics blocking and simple.)
258	- Detectors run on their own FreeRTOS tasks (one per detector instance) so a slow detector cannot stall the frame pipeline.
259	
260	#### 4.2.5 Reference-detector responsibilities
261	
262	`cv_marvin_v1` is a *first-class* subsystem, not a debug aid. Its detector state is the ground-truth label for any reference-data recording (§4.6). Implications:
263	
264	- Algorithm changes are versioned (`cv_marvin_v1`, `cv_marvin_v2`, …). The version is stamped into recordings so training data stays attributable.
265	- Calibration (sensor/strike-line ROIs in pixel space) is stored in the system config (§4.7) and reproducibly applied at startup.
266	- The detector must run within one frame-time (≤ 16.7 ms) on Cortex-A5 — concrete algorithm choice is a future decision, but the budget is set.
267	
268	#### 4.2.6 Open questions surfaced here
269	
270	- Initial CV algorithm — pixel-mean threshold per ROI, edge-trough, optical-flow-based, or learned. (Defer; bring up the simplest first to validate end-to-end.)
271	- ADC-detector logic location — port `fretboard/fret_button.c`'s detection (hysteresis edges) into marvin (`adc_fretboard` runs on raw samples), or have fretboard pre-process and stream edges. (Default: marvin runs the detector on raw samples; fretboard stays dumb.)
272	
273	### 4.3 Fretboard link ✅
274	
275	Direct **FLEXCOM1 USART** link between marvin and the fretboard MCU — a plain UART wire, no USB. marvin's `PA28` (FLEXCOM1_IO0, `GUITAR_TX`) and `PA29` (FLEXCOM1_IO1, `GUITAR_RX`) connect to the fretboard's SERCOM1 (`PB01` RX / `PB00` TX). Both ends run **500 000 baud, 8N1**. The FLEXCOM1 USART runs in Harmony ring-buffer mode so RX never drops bytes between reads. (Was FLEXCOM2 until the console moved onto FLEXCOM2 — see §4.9.)
276	
277	- **Marvin → fretboard:** command bitmask (which frets to assert + strum direction). 1-byte bitmask, no framing. `fretboard_link_task` writes the latest mask via `FLEXCOM1_USART_Write`.
278	- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 240 Hz, in a 17-byte start/end-bracketed frame (`0x03 … 0xFC`, with `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`). The FLEXCOM1 RX ring fills continuously from its ISR; a persistent read-threshold notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which drains the ring, resyncs on the frame markers, and republishes each valid frame as a `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` perf-log record (default-disabled, host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`). This is the on-board capture path until the SD-card recorder lands; it's also the substrate for the future `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2).
279	- **Standalone fallback:** when marvin's timing pipeline is disabled (see §4.4 and §6), the fretboard runs its own existing chord FIFO (`fret_button.c`) and continues to stream ADC + emitted-command telemetry to marvin for capture/display.
280	
281	### 4.4 Timing pipeline 🚧
282	
283	Centralized on marvin by default. Owns:
284	
285	- Chord-accumulation window (`CHORD_WINDOW_MS` ≈ 20–40 ms).
286	- Pending-chord FIFO with per-chord `press_at` / `strum_at` ticks.
287	- Per-fret release scheduling.
288	- Strum direction alternation and pulse generation.
289	- `STRUM_DELAY_MS` / `FRET_EARLY_MS` / `STRUM_PULSE_MS` constants — initial values port from `tools/fret-tuner/SPEC.md` and `firmware/fretboard/SPEC.md`.
290	
291	**Disable / handoff mode:** an operator-mode toggle (§6) deactivates marvin's pipeline. fretboard then runs its own existing pipeline; marvin still ingests ADC + emitted-command telemetry for recording/display, but does not emit commands.
292	
293	### 4.5 UI / operator surface 🚧
294	
295	10.1″ 1280×800 LVDS panel + maxtouch capacitive touch. Functional surfaces required:
296	
297	- Live game view (capture composited with detector overlays — sensor crosshairs, detection events, latency markers).
298	- Calibration / tuning (per-fret ROI placement, threshold values, timing constants).
299	- Mode + run controls (idle, calibrate, dry-run, play, replay, record).
300	- Logs / history / stats (recent commands, miss/hit counts, dropped frames).
301	
302	**UI framework — open Q5.** Legato is already pulled in for capture init and could absorb the operator UI directly (heavy but in-tree). Alternative: a lightweight custom widget layer over GFX2D / direct framebuffer composition. Decision deferred until we attempt the first non-trivial screen (calibration overlay).
303	
304	### 4.6 Reference-data recording & export 🚧
305	
306	#### 4.6.1 Goals (in priority order)
307	
308	1. **Edge-AI training data** — produce labelled frames + ground-truth detector state suitable for training low-fidelity detectors (fretboard's photo-detector logic; future Edge-AI MCU).
309	2. **Replay / sanity check** — let the user (offline) scrub through a recorded session to investigate misses.
310	3. **Multi-detector sync** — independent detectors (fretboard ADC, future Edge-AI) record their own data alongside marvin's; everyone sync's on a shared frame epoch.
311	
312	Live off-device streaming for side-by-side comparison is *not* on the MVP critical path.
313	
314	#### 4.6.2 Transport — SD card
315	
316	Recordings are persisted to an SD card via SDMMC + a simple filesystem (FAT32 via Harmony's FILE_SYSTEM service). The card is removed and read on a workstation; no live network path is required for MVP.
317	
318	Bandwidth ceiling: SDMMC sustained write ≥ 5 MB/s on Class-10 cards is reliably achievable. The recording format below is sized to land well below that.
319	
320	#### 4.6.3 Format — detector-state + sparse keyframes
321	
322	A recording is a **directory** on the SD card, containing:
323	
324	```
325	recordings/
326	└── 2026-05-20T14-32-08/
327	    ├── manifest.json          // session metadata, calibration snapshot, detector versions
328	    ├── state.bin              // dense detector_state_t records, all detectors, all frames
329	    ├── commands.bin           // emitted fret/strum commands with frame_epoch
330	    ├── adc_raw.bin            // raw fretboard ADC stream with frame_epoch interleave
331	    └── keyframes/
332	        ├── 000000.bgr         // raw BGR888 keyframe (no encoder), filename = frame_epoch
333	        ├── 000060.bgr
334	        └── ...
335	```
336	
337	- **`state.bin`** — append-only, fixed-size `detector_state_t` records (§4.2.3). At 60 Hz × 2 detectors × ~28 B = ~3.4 KB/s. Trivial.
338	- **`commands.bin`** — fret/strum bitmask + direction + emit timestamp + frame_epoch, ~16 B per emit. Sparse.
339	- **`adc_raw.bin`** — fretboard 17-byte frames at 240 Hz with `frame_epoch` annotation = ~4.1 KB/s. Modest. Until the SD recorder lands, the same data is available live as `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` records (28 B framed) in any marvin-perf capture (default-disabled; enable with `set-mask`).
340	- **Keyframes** — raw BGR888 packed dump every N captured frames. At 720×480 × 3 B = 1.04 MB/keyframe. Default cadence: **1 keyframe per second** (60-frame stride) → 1.04 MB/s sustained. Configurable (every 30 / 60 / 120 / 600 frames). At 1 fps a 5-minute session is ~312 MB — comfortable on any modern SD card.
341	- No software JPEG / video encode. SAM9X75 has no hardware JPEG; CPU encode at 60 fps is infeasible. Keyframes stay raw; offline tools can transcode if desired.
342	
343	Filename convention: directory name is ISO-8601 timestamp at session start (UTC); keyframe filenames are zero-padded `frame_epoch` so chronological order matches lexical order.
344	
345	#### 4.6.4 Sync token — `frame_epoch`
346	
347	A 32-bit counter incremented by the video task on every captured ISC frame (rolls over after ~830 days @ 60 Hz). Every record in a session — `state.bin`, `commands.bin`, `adc_raw.bin`, keyframe filenames, off-board detector data — is keyed by `frame_epoch`. This is the master clock for the entire system, including any later-added detectors that record independently and need to align their data with marvin's.
348	
349	For records that don't fall on a frame boundary (ADC samples emitted between video frames), the most-recent `frame_epoch` is used and the sub-frame offset is captured by `timestamp_us`.
350	
351	#### 4.6.5 manifest.json
352	
353	Minimum fields:
354	
355	```json
356	{
357	  "schema_version": 1,
358	  "session_started_utc": "2026-05-20T14:32:08Z",
359	  "marvin_firmware_git": "<hash>",
360	  "capture": { "width": 720, "height": 480, "fps": 60, "format": "BGR888" },
361	  "keyframe_stride_frames": 60,
362	  "detectors": [
363	    { "id": "cv_marvin_v1", "version": "1.0.0", "calibration": { ... } },
364	    { "id": "adc_fretboard", "version": "1.0.0", "thresholds": { ... } }
365	  ],
366	  "timing": { "chord_window_ms": 20, "strum_delay_ms": 220, "fret_early_ms": 50, "strum_pulse_ms": 50 },
367	  "ended_utc": null
368	}
369	```
370	
371	Written at session start; `ended_utc` is patched on a clean stop.
372	
373	#### 4.6.6 On-device buffering
374	
375	A FreeRTOS task (`record_task`) owns SD writes. State / command / ADC streams are small and write through directly. Keyframes are larger — a single keyframe at 1.04 MB cannot block the video pipeline, so the record task receives a **frame buffer pointer** (the same DDR buffer the ISC writes into; refcounted by the video task) and writes from DDR while the next frame is being captured into another buffer. We need ≥ 3 capture frame buffers (one capturing, one displaying, one being recorded) when recording is active; today the video task already has multiple frames pre-allocated — exact count is verified during implementation.
376	
377	If the SD write FIFO falls behind (rare; only a sustained-throughput problem), the recorder drops keyframes (logs a `RECORD_DROP` event into `state.bin`'s metadata channel) but **never** drops detector-state records.
378	
379	#### 4.6.7 Off-board detectors recording independently
380	
381	When a future Edge-AI detection unit is brought online, it can:
382	
383	- Subscribe to marvin's `frame_epoch` over a chosen link (UART/Ethernet/etc.).
384	- Record its own observations (e.g. its own sensor data + its own detector output) in its own format, *keyed by marvin's `frame_epoch`*.
385	- Be aligned post-hoc against marvin's reference recording during training.
386	
387	The spec does not constrain how off-board detectors store their data — only the sync contract (`frame_epoch` timeline) is canonical.
388	
389	#### 4.6.8 On-demand full-frame snapshot (USB CDC) ✅
390	
391	Independent of the SD recording path above (M4, not started), marvin can export a single full-resolution frame on demand over the existing perf-log USB CDC link. The host sends `PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT`; the perf-drain task copies the current frame once into a staging buffer and streams it back as a top-to-bottom run of full-width `PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT` band records (each ≤ `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES`), all sharing one `frame_epoch`, the last flagged `PERF_STRIP_FLAG_LAST`. Bands are written straight to the sink (bypassing the small strip pool) and paced by the wire; emit is not gated by the STRIP type mask. `marvin-perf snapshot` reassembles and saves the frame (`.bgr` + sidecar `.json`, plus `.png` via Pillow). This is the offline-study on-ramp for the game-state work (§4.8) — no in-runtime role.
392	
393	### 4.7 System services 🚧
394	
395	Cross-cutting services not owned by any one subsystem:
396	
397	- **Logging** ✅ severity-filtered printf shim (commit `a79042f`).
398	- **Time** ✅ TC0 / SYS_TIME for OSAL.
399	- **Config persistence** 🚧 calibration values, mode toggles, last-used recording stride. Storage TBD (a config file on SD vs internal flash).
400	- **Watchdog** 🚧 not yet enabled.
401	- **OTA** ⚪ out of scope for now.
402	
403	### 4.8 Game-state awareness & control 🚧
404	
405	Note on numbering: this subsystem is logically a peer of §4.2–§4.6 (a video-frame consumer that emits typed events plus a controller that issues actuator commands). It lives at §4.8 only to avoid renumbering existing sections referenced from the journal and milestones.
406	
407	#### 4.8.1 Role
408	
409	Two related capabilities, both grounded in CV on the captured video stream:
410	
411	1. **Game-state observer.** Watch the screen; recognize what context the game is currently in — main menu, song-select, difficulty-select, in-game (gameplay), pause, score summary, etc. Surface that as typed events that the operator UI can render and the orchestrator below can act on.
412	2. **Game controller.** Expose high-level verbs ("start a single-player playthrough of song X on Hard", "go to the main menu", "select Practice mode"). Translate each verb into a sequence of fret/strum commands using the recognized current state and a known menu graph, monitor the screen for the expected state transitions, retry or back out on mismatch.
413	
414	This is *not* the gameplay note-detection path (§4.2). cv_marvin_v1 plays notes during gameplay; the game-state module decides *what to play* at the session level (which song, which difficulty, which mode) and gets us there from any starting screen.
415	
416	Recognition is bootstrapped offline: the on-demand snapshot path (§4.6.8) collects a corpus of real GH3 screens, detection algorithms are prototyped host-side in Python (`tools/gameplay/`) against that corpus, and only the proven GH3-specific logic is ported into the firmware `gameplay_engine` module. Per Q10, the approach favors fixed-region/color/glyph matching over general CV — GH3's screens, fonts, and layouts are static.
417	
418	**M9 progress:** Phase 1 (screen-context classifier: main_menu / song_select / gameplay / pause / score) and Phase 2 (section-select and song-name readers) are prototyped and ported to firmware (`gameplay_engine.c`); the MPLAB build is confirmed. Phase 3 (number/score readers) is not yet started. The firmware module is pending hardware validation.
419	
420	#### 4.8.2 Module shape
421	
422	- Owns its own FreeRTOS task (`game_task`).
423	- Subscribes to the video frame queue via the same multi-subscriber API used by detectors (§4.2.4); it is a video-frame consumer, **not** a detector. Its events do not flow on `xDetectorStateQueue`.
424	- Emits typed events on a separate, narrow bus (`xGameStateQueue`) — current_state changes, ambiguity warnings, error states.
425	- Orchestrator state for high-level verbs (current goal, expected next state, retry counter) lives inside `game_task`.
426	- Issues control commands by writing fret/strum bitmasks into the same fretboard-link path used by gameplay. Whether this routes through the timing pipeline (§4.4) or bypasses it is open Q11.
427	
428	#### 4.8.3 Game catalog & menu metadata
429	
430	The recognizer and the navigator both depend on per-game data:
431	
432	- **Recognizer templates.** Per-state visual signatures used by the CV recognizer — could be small reference images (template matching), color histograms, or text regions for OCR. Format chosen with the recognizer algorithm (open Q10).
433	- **Menu graph.** Nodes = recognized game states; edges = button sequences that move between them (e.g., "main_menu → song_select" = `[STRUM_DOWN, STRUM_DOWN, GREEN]`). Used by the navigator to plan a verb.
434	- **Song catalog.** Per-supported-game list of songs with the menu coordinates needed to select each one (which difficulty submenu, ordinal position in the list, etc.). Possibly augmented with metadata (BPM, length, expected difficulty score) for UI display and for reference-data labeling.
435	
436	Storage: compile-time tables for the per-game graph + a JSON or similar on the SD card for songlists and any user-editable bits. Exact split deferred until first concrete game is added.
437	
438	Scope today: target is **one game** — Guitar Hero (Wii) — to validate the design. Adding a second game is a metadata addition (new template set + new menu graph + new song catalog), not a structural change.
439	
440	#### 4.8.4 Interaction with other subsystems
441	
442	- **Detection (§4.2):** independent. cv_marvin_v1 runs only when the game-state observer reports `gameplay`. Outside gameplay, cv_marvin_v1 may be disabled to free CPU.
443	- **Timing pipeline (§4.4):** during gameplay the timing pipeline drives the actuators from detector-state. Outside gameplay it's idle, and the game-state controller drives actuators directly. Coordination and arbitration between the two is open Q11.
444	- **Operator UI (§4.5):** consumes game-state events to display the current screen the game is on; offers verbs as buttons / song-list pickers.
445	- **Recording (§4.6):** game-state transitions are useful session metadata. Either annotated into `state.bin` as a side channel or a sibling file (`game_state.bin`). To be decided when the recorder lands.
446	- **Fretboard link (§4.3):** shared command path. The fretboard MCU does not know whether a press is "gameplay note" or "menu navigation" — they're the same wire bits.
447	
448	#### 4.8.5 Open questions surfaced here
449	
450	See §9 for tracking entries. In summary:
451	
452	- **Q10** — Recognizer algorithm: template matching vs simple OCR vs region/color heuristics vs a small CNN. Trade-off is robustness vs CPU cost vs metadata authoring effort.
453	- **Q11** — Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline. Default is "they don't run at the same time" (gameplay vs menu), but the boundary needs to be explicit.
454	
455	### 4.9 Operator command console ✅
456	
457	An **interactive text console** over **FLEXCOM2 USART (115 200 8N1, ring-buffer mode)** — marvin's `PA13` (FLEXCOM2_IO0, `CLI_TX`) / `PA14` (FLEXCOM2_IO1, `CLI_RX`) — deliberately on a separate channel from the DBGU log/printf chatter — log output stays on DBGU, console I/O stays on FLEXCOM2, so neither pollutes the other.
458	
459	- **Why not Harmony `SYS_CONSOLE`/`SYS_COMMAND`:** those are MCC-config-coupled and live in regenerated files (this board already carries ~10 re-apply patches against clobbered generated code). 461	- **Mechanics:** one FreeRTOS task drains the FLEXCOM2 RX ring (woken by a 1-byte read-threshold notification, like `fretboard_rx_task`), feeds bytes to embedded-cli, and runs the dispatcher. Output is written byte-by-byte into the TX ring.
462	- **Commands (v0):** `status`, `detect <cv|adc> <on|off>`, `active <cv|adc>`, `timing <on|off>`, `manual <on|off>`, `fret <g|r|y|b|o> <0|1>`, `strum <down|up>` — dispatching into the existing `Detector_*`, `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled`, and `ManualControl_*` setters. The binding table is a plain static array; adding a command is one row. Maps onto the §6 operating-mode toggles. (b) Timing FIFO on marvin, not fretboard: marvin already runs the canonical detector and the recording pipeline, so co-locating timing keeps a single source of truth and avoids re-deriving state on the actuator side. Spec §4.4. The fretboard-takeover fallback (spec §6) is a separate mode where marvin disables its pipeline and fretboard runs `fret_button.c` standalone — that's the high-availability path, not the steady-state. (c) 1-byte bitmask matches `tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py` and `firmware/fretboard/cmd_receive.h` exactly (G/R/Y/B/O at bits 0..4, strum-down bit 5, strum-up bit 6) — no reason to invent a new framing while the protocol is this small. Future paths considered: (1) marvin compensates by subtracting a fretboard-published latency from `assert_at`/`strum_at`; (2) fretboard compensates by accepting timestamped events and scheduling locally. 113	- **`vApplicationStackOverflowHook` is a silent infinite-loop.** ([freertos_hooks.c:62-76](../default/src/config/default/freertos_hooks.c#L62-L76)) MCC's default is `taskDISABLE_INTERRUPTS()` then `for (;;)`. An actual overflow is indistinguishable from any other freeze on hardware. Patch the hook to emit a `LOG_ERR` line naming the offending task before the spin (carefully — the stack is already corrupt, so the hook should avoid using locals or large stack frames). Already nearly bit us once: 2026-05-21 freeze in `open_cdc()` was first misdiagnosed as a stack overflow because we had no visibility into actual stack usage of the FBL task. (HWM/RUNTIME records reach the host now post-2026-05-29 work, so we have *steady-state* stack visibility — but a real overflow still freezes silently.)

With the manual-control surface adding 8 buttons and frequent press/release events during menu nav, confirm `legato_config.h` `LE_MEMORY_MANAGER_SIZE` has headroom for typical event bursts. Watch for Legato heap-exhaustion symptoms (silent dropped events, widget redraw glitches) once the UI is exercised on hardware.

If a second Legato screen is ever added, `ManualInput_Bind` must re-run inside that screen's show path (or whichever screen owns the manual-control widgets). Not an issue today — flagged for whenever the operator UI grows beyond Screen0.

Keyframe size corrected to 1.04 MB (720×480 × 3). README.md updated with project intro.

121	- **MCC-file modifications maintenance risk.** A from-scratch MCC regen on 2026-05-15 confirmed **four** local modifications get clobbered. The 2026-05-20 USB-host regen added a fifth. Re-apply after every regen:
122	
123	  1. **`plib_csi.c` — `CSI_Analog_Init` refactor.** MCC emits per-lane HS-RX init inline with three bugs: Lane 1 in the 2-lane branch is missing the bit-rate write, Lane 2's lane-select code is `0x24` instead of `0x64`, and the 4-lane else-if branch skips Lane 1 entirely. Replace with the `csi_phy_hs_rx_init(lane_code, bit_rate)` helper and call it for lanes 0/1/2/3 from a flat `if (nlanes >= …)` chain.
124	
125	  2. **`plib_xlcdc.c` `XLCDC_EnableClocks` — `PMC_PLL_ACR`.** Set to datasheet-optimal `0x12023010` for the LVDSPLL with our 24 MHz reference (in the `fIN ∈ [20 MHz, 32 MHz]` band). Specifically: `LOOP_FILTER=0x12, LOCK_THR=0x2, UTMIBG=1, UTMIVR=1, CONTROL=0x10`. MCC's default emits a different (less-optimal) analog config (`LOOP_FILTER=0x1B, LOCK_THR=0x4, no UTMI bits`). Doesn't affect functional behavior in our use (50 Hz refresh works either way), but is the manufacturer-recommended jitter/lock optimum.
126	
127	  3. **`plib_csi2dc.c` `CSI2DC_Configure_VideoPipe` — `| CSI2DC_VPCFGR_RMS_1`.** Required by the RGB888-packed capture path: byte-stream packs 4 BGR pixels across 12 bytes per CSI-2 RMS spec (Table 49.27). Without it, capture writes wrong-format bytes and the display shows garbage. *(Earlier journal note claimed this was now MCC's default — incorrect; this regen confirmed MCC still emits without RMS_1.)*
128	
129	  4. **`drv_image_sensor.h` enum shim.** MCC's regen *deletes* this file when the image-sensor component is disabled. Restore the 30-line shim at `default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/image_sensor/drv_image_sensor.h` defining `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_RAW_BAYER…JPEG` and `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_8_BIT…40_BIT` enums (numeric values must match the original — `drv_isc.c` derives `bits_per_pixel = 4 - inputBits`). Without it, `drv_isc.c` and `configuration.h` won't compile.
130	
131	  5. **`initialization.c` `SYS_Initialize` — peripheral init order.** **(Hybrid board: the peripheral is now `FLEXCOM8_TWI_Initialize` (not FLEXCOM6) and there's no USB-host regen, but the MMU/AIC-before-peripherals concern still stands — verified intact on 2026-06-08: MMU/AIC run before TC0/FLEXCOM2/FLEXCOM8/XLCDC.)** The USB-host MCC regen (2026-05-20) reordered SYS_Initialize so that `TC0_CH0_TimerInitialize`, `FLEXCOM6_TWI_Initialize`, and `XLCDC_Initialize` run *before* `MMU_Initialize` and `AIC_INT_Initialize`. Symptom on hardware: TC358743 probe wedges on its first I²C write — `OSAL_SEM_Pend(transferDone, WAIT_FOREVER)` never returns because the FLEXCOM6 ISR never fires. (Display + capture totally dead; FBL heartbeat keeps printing because it doesn't depend on a peripheral interrupt.) Fix: move the `MMU_Initialize → AIC_INT_Initialize → WDT-disable` block back to *before* the TC0/FLEXCOM6/XLCDC inits, matching the pre-USB-regen order. After this revert, video came back immediately. Resolved on 2026-05-20.
132	
133	  6. **`FreeRTOSConfig.h` — `portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS` / `portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE` macros + 64-bit counter type.** With `configGENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS = 1` (set via `FREERTOS_GENERATE_RUN_TIME_STATS` MCC symbol), FreeRTOS expects the application to provide a free-running counter. MCC's FreeRTOS Harmony component does not expose a knob for an app-specific counter source. Append at the end of `FreeRTOSConfig.h` (just before `#endif`):
134	     ```c
135	     extern uint64_t SYS_TIME_Counter64Get(void);
136	     #define configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE             uint64_t
137	     #define portCONFIGURE_TIMER_FOR_RUN_TIME_STATS()
138	     #define portGET_RUN_TIME_COUNTER_VALUE()        SYS_TIME_Counter64Get()
139	     ```
140	     `SYS_TIME` is already initialised by Harmony before the scheduler starts, so the configure macro is a no-op. `SYS_TIME_Counter64Get` returns the full 64-bit TC0 CH0 counter; the matching `configRUN_TIME_COUNTER_TYPE = uint64_t` overrides FreeRTOS's `uint32_t` default so cumulative `ulRunTimeCounter` values don't wrap (uint32_t at 266 MHz wraps after ~16 s of accumulated CPU time across all tasks, which made percentages garbage almost immediately). Bare `extern` (rather than including a Harmony header) keeps `FreeRTOSConfig.h` consumable by low-level kernel sources that don't pull in `definitions.h`.
141	
142	  7. **`drv_usb_udphs_device.c` — multi-IRP DMA arming in completion ISRs.** Stock UDPHS device driver only programs the DMA channel in `IRPSubmit`'s queue-empty branch (line 1604+); IRPs appended to a non-empty queue link in (line 2273-2284 of patched file via `iterator->next = irp_t`) but never get armed for transmission. `Tasks_ISR_DMA` advances `irpQueue = irp->next` after firing the callback but does not re-program DMA hardware. Result: only one IRP per "queue idle" sequence ever transmits — the rest sit `STATUS_PENDING` forever.
143	
144	      Fix is additive (no refactor of working code): add a static helper `F_DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_ArmDmaForIrp` just before `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit`, mirroring the existing inline DMA-program block (~80 lines covering both DEVICE_TO_HOST and HOST_TO_DEVICE directions). Then add a call after the queue advance in **two** places:
145	
146	      - `Tasks_ISR_DMA` immediately after `endpointObj->irpQueue = irp->next; irp->callback(...)` — the normal DMA-completion path.
147	      - The ZLP-completion path inside `Tasks_ISR` (under "endpoint interrupt on a DMA capable endpoint, so it should be a ZLP"), same place: after queue advance.
148	
149	      Both call sites guarded by `if (endpointObj->irpQueue != NULL)`. Patch markers `/* PATCH: */` make the change findable after MCC regen. Helper carries the same cache-clean and DMA-program shape as the inline original, including the `__DSB(); __ISB();` barriers and the `SYS_CACHE_CleanDCache_by_Addr` for the IRP data buffer.
150	
151	      Without this patch, the lever-1 multi-IRP work (`queueSizeWrite=3`, `USB_DEVICE_CDC_QUEUE_DEPTH_COMBINED=5`) accepts writes but only ever transmits the first of any batch. With it, multi-IRP pipelining works as designed at the driver level. Patch is specific to Harmony USB v3.16.0 device driver; check whether future versions wire the post-completion arm and obviate the patch.
152	
153	  8. **`driver/input/drv_maxtouch.c` — bounded maXTouch init so an absent touch panel can't hang the whole system.** Stock `mxt_initialize()` does `while (1) { mxt_read_info_block(); if (!error) break; }`. With the display/maXTouch panel disconnected the info-block read never succeeds, so it spins forever — and because each `mxt_read_info_block()` allocates from the FreeRTOS heap (heap_1, no free), the retries leak until the heap is exhausted and the system hangs in `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. This is exactly what blocked the JTAG load-to-RAM bring-up (fault landed in `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks`, `xNextFreeByte`=40,944/40,960). Three-part fix: (a) `__mxt_read_reg` now propagates the real `DRV_I2C_WriteReadTransfer` result (`? 0 : -EIO`) instead of hardcoding `ret = 0`, so a NAK from an absent controller is detected at the *first* read and bails before the second, garbage-sized `OSAL_Malloc`; (b) `mxt_initialize` retries at most `MXT_INIT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (10, 20 ms apart) then returns the error; (c) `DRV_MAXTOUCH_Tasks` `DEVICE_STATE_MXT_INITIALIZE` parks the driver in `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR` (not READY) on failure, so the rest of the system runs headless without touch. Syntax-checked clean with XC32 v4.60, then **validated on hardware (2026-06-08)**: with the display/maXTouch panel disconnected, marvin loaded via the JTAG load-to-RAM flow now boots *past* maXTouch init (driver → `DEVICE_STATE_ERROR`) and runs headless — PC samples land in `DRV_USB_UDPHS_DEVICE_IRPSubmit` / `USB_DEVICE_CDC_Read` (perf-log USB-CDC path) and advance across the codebase, instead of hanging at `vApplicationMallocFailedHook`. Re-apply after every maXTouch MCC regen.

```text
1	# Fretboard Firmware Specification
2	
3	> **Re-scoped to a T1S sense+actuate node (2026-06-17):** the fretboard is a 10BASE-T1S
4	> PLCA follower (id 1) that infers actuator commands from the phototransistor data and drives the
5	> [`guitar`](../guitar/SPEC.md) node over T1S, while also streaming its data to marvin. The old UART
6	> link, the standalone Wii-guitar GPIO outputs (`cmd_receive.c`), and the `FRETBOARD_LINK`/`FRETBOARD_MODE`
7	> build flags are gone — one behaviour. Node-class model: top-level [`SPEC.md`](../../SPEC.md) §2; link
8	> detail: [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md).
9	
10	## Overview
11	
12	Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz). The fretboard is a 10BASE-T1S
13	node that both **senses** and **drives**. Each 240 Hz tick it samples five
14	phototransistors above the TV strike line; an on-device int8 neural net
15	(`model_infer.c`, weights in the generated `model_weights.h`) infers the Wii-guitar
16	button bitmask from the ADC window. Over T1S it then:
17	
18	- **streams** the 17-byte data frame (ADC scan + the driven bitmask) to the marvin
19	  coordinator — logging / edge-ai training; and
20	- **commands** the [`guitar`](../guitar/SPEC.md) node (id 2) directly with the
21	  inferred bitmask — peer-to-peer actuation; marvin coordinates/logs but is out of
22	  the command path.
23	
24	Inference runs in the main loop (it overruns the 240 Hz tick in the ISR); the ISR
25	only scans + stages the data frame. SW0 arms actuation, LED0 shows armed (boots
26	disarmed → commands 0/released). It has **no local Wii-guitar outputs** — those pins
27	are the LAN8651 SPI. See [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md), edge-ai
28	[`runtime.md`](../../tools/edge-ai/docs/runtime.md), and
29	[`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md).
30	
31	## Hardware
32	
33	### Target
34	
35	| Spec | Value |
36	|------|-------|
37	| Device | PIC32CM6408PL10048 |
38	| Core | ARM Cortex-M0+ |
39	| Clock | 24 MHz |
40	| Toolchain | XC32 5.10 |
41	| Programmer | PKOB nano |
42	
43	### Pin Map
44	
45	#### Sensor Inputs (ADC)
46	
47	Five phototransistors positioned above the TV strike line. Each
48	produces an analog voltage that drops when a note passes the sensor.
49	ADC reads 12-bit unsigned (0–4095); lower values indicate note
50	presence.
51	
52	| Channel | ADC Input | Pin |
53	|---------|-----------|-----|
54	| Green | AIN28 | PA28 |
55	| Red | AIN16 | PA16 |
56	| Yellow | AIN19 | PA19 |
57	| Blue | AIN27 | PA27 |
58	| Orange | AIN26 | PA26 |
59	
60	There are no button/strum outputs — those GPIOs are the LAN8651 SPI/CS/IRQ/RST
61	pins now. See [`t1s_detector.c`](t1s_detector.c).
62	
63	#### SERCOM0 SPI — LAN8651 (T1S)
64	
65	Mode 0 (CPOL=0/CPHA=0, MSB, 8-bit): MOSI=PA04, SCK=PA05, MISO=PA07; `T1S_CS`=PA15
66	(GPIO, held low across each TC6 chunk), `T1S_RST`=PA14, `T1S_IRQ_N`=PA13 (EIC
67	EXTINT13, falling).
68	
69	#### SERCOM1 — operator console
70	
71	Hosts the embedded-cli console + diagnostic log. TX PB00 / RX PB01, **500 000** 8N1,
72	ring-buffer mode (TX ring ≥ 512 B).
73	
74	## Software Architecture
75	
76	### Processing Loop
77	
78	`TC0` fires a periodic callback at **240 Hz** (≈4.17 ms). The ISR scans and stages
79	the data frame with the currently-driven command; the heavy work (inference, TC6
80	service, TX flush) runs in the `main()` service loop:
81	
82	```
83	TC0 ISR (240 Hz)                     main() service loop
84	  fret_scan_all()                      model_infer_* -> s_latest_cmd
85	  push sample to model queue           T1SDetector_SetCommand(cmd) -> guitar (T1S)
86	  cmd = armed ? s_latest_cmd : 0       T1SDetector_Tasks()  (service + flush data + HB)
87	  data_stream_send(cmd)  (stage)       CLI_Tasks()
88	```
89	
90	The ISR stays short (the model overruns the tick if run there — see the journal /
91	edge-ai `runtime.md` §3). `data_stream_send()` stages the frame; `T1SDetector_Tasks()`
92	flushes it (and the guitar command, and the heartbeat) from the main loop.
93	
94	### Module Descriptions
95	
96	#### fret_scan ([fret_scan.c](fret_scan.c) / [fret_scan.h](fret_scan.h))
97	
98	Reads all five ADC channels sequentially using blocking polling.
99	Results are stored in a static array and accessed via
100	`fret_scan_result(channel)`.
101	
102	The channel enum defines the canonical fret ordering used throughout
103	the firmware:
104	
105	```
106	FRET_GREEN = 0, FRET_RED = 1, FRET_YELLOW = 2, FRET_BLUE = 3, FRET_ORANGE = 4
107	```
108	
109	#### data_stream ([data_stream.c](data_stream.c) / [data_stream.h](data_stream.h))
110	
111	Builds one 17-byte little-endian frame per tick and stages it for TX to the marvin
112	coordinator over T1S (via `T1SDetector_SendFrame`):
113	
114	| Offset | Size | Field |
115	|-------:|-----:|-------|
116	| 0 | 1 | start = `0x03` |
117	| 1 | 2 | green (uint16) |
118	| 3 | 2 | red |
119	| 5 | 2 | yellow |
120	| 7 | 2 | blue |
121	| 9 | 2 | orange |
122	| 11 | 4 | sample_seq (uint32) — monotonic, one per tick |
123	| 15 | 1 | applied_mask — the bitmask driven to the guitar this scan |
124	| 16 | 1 | end = `0xFC` (`~start`) |
125	
126	`sample_seq` lets the host reconstruct true sample order and detect dropped frames
127	(it advances per tick even when a send is skipped). `applied_mask` is the command
128	the node drove to the guitar this scan, paired atomically with the ADC scan for
129	edge-ai training-data export. The marvin RX side keys on this 17-byte layout.
130	
131	### T1S node ([t1s_detector.c](t1s_detector.c) / [.h](t1s_detector.h))
132	
133	PLCA follower **id 1**, MAC `02:00:00:00:00:01`, on the marvin-coordinated
134	(`02:..:00`) bus via a LAN8651 MAC-PHY over SERCOM0 SPI. Reuses the shared
135	`third_party/oa-tc6-lib` (OPEN Alliance TC6) + a local `tc6-conf.h`. All TC6 access
136	is serviced from the **main loop** (`T1SDetector_Tasks()`), never the 240 Hz ISR.
137	
138	- **Data → coordinator:** the 17-byte frame rides the Ethernet payload under
139	  ethertype `0x88B5`, dst = coordinator MAC. The ISR stages it
140	  (`T1SDetector_SendFrame()`, latest-wins); the main loop flushes it, one TX in
141	  flight. A frame dropped while busy shows as a `sample_seq` gap.
142	- **Command → guitar:** `T1SDetector_SetCommand()` (main loop) hands the inferred
143	  1-byte bitmask to the **guitar node** (id 2, MAC `02:..:02`, ethertype `0x88B5`).
144	  Sent edge-triggered + re-sent every 50 ms so a dropped command self-heals; the
145	  guitar applies latest-wins. Peer-to-peer — marvin is not in the command path.
146	- **Presence:** a 500 ms heartbeat (ethertype `0x88B6`, `node_type = 1` detector) so
147	  marvin's `nodes` command shows the node present.
148	- **Operator CLI:** SERCOM1 hosts an embedded-cli console ([cli.c](cli.c), vendored
149	  `third_party/embedded-cli/`): `t1s` (link / sync / chipRev / PLCA / data+command tx
150	  counts), `adc` (latest scan), `id` / `plca` (MAC-PHY register diagnostics).
151	  Bare-metal — `CLI_Tasks()` drains the RX ring each main-loop pass.
152	
153	**Coordination caveat:** there is no active-source arbitration yet — while the
154	fretboard is armed (SW0) it drives the guitar, and marvin must not also command the
155	guitar (both target `02:..:02`). marvin-side active-detector/active-guitar selection
156	is the follow-up. Link rationale, addressing, and the PoDL plan are in
157	[`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md).
158	
159	## Observability
160	
161	The data stream lands on **marvin** now (over T1S), so health is read there: the
162	`PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` rate via [`tools/marvin-perf`](../../tools/marvin-perf/) and

Leave it. To reduce the *new* T1S transport delay instead, raise the host SPI clock (1 MHz → ~12 MHz, both fretboard and guitar; SERCOM `BAUD=0` = GCLK/2 = 12 MHz) and/or fold a constant offset into the training labels — **not** by changing the command-to-tick coupling. | The model's timing was characterized against this inference→tick→actuate pipeline (the photo-dip→strum delay is baked into the distillation labels, so its output index is fit to *this* cadence). Decoupling would shift every actuation earlier by up to a tick **and** replace the deterministic 240 Hz grid with main-loop jitter — for a model trained on 240 Hz-sampled data, consistent grid-aligned latency beats lower-but-variable latency. Separately, the T1S move already changed timing vs. the old `MODEL_DRIVEN` *local-GPIO* standalone: actuation is now ~1.5–2 ms **later** (host-SPI chunk each end @ 1 MHz dominates; PLCA media access is sub-ms). That transport delta — not the tick — is the real new variable, so the knob is SPI speed (12 MHz removes ~1 ms) + re-validating gameplay timing on the T1S rig (scope fretboard `SetCommand`→guitar apply, check hit rate). Worst-case command latency today ≈ 6–7 ms (≈4.2 ms tick + ~1.5–2 ms transport); ~2–3 ms typical. See edge-ai journal + [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md). |

57	
58	1. **No corruption signalling on the wire.** A bit-flip inside the 5 uint16 payload bytes is silently accepted — only out-of-range start/end bytes are caught. 1	# guitar — Specification
2	
3	> What guitar *is* (purpose, hardware, interfaces, firmware design, milestones).
4	> The running diary of decisions and progress lives in [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) — read it alongside this on any non-trivial task.
5	
6	> **Status: working on hardware.** The T1S PLCA follower is up (chipRev read, link
7	> synced), receives marvin's command over T1S and actuates the Wii GPIOs, sends a
8	> presence heartbeat, and exposes a debug-UART CLI. Remaining work is the full
9	> multi-node system (G3) — see §6 and [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md).
10	
11	## 1. Purpose
12	
13	guitar is the **Wii-guitar actuator node** on the marvin T1S bus. It receives a 1-byte
14	button bitmask from [marvin](../marvin/docs/spec.md) over 10BASE-T1S and drives a real Wii
15	guitar controller's buttons via open-drain GPIO. It does **no sensing and no game logic** —
16	it is purely the actuation half of what today's [fretboard](../fretboard/SPEC.md) firmware
17	does, lifted onto its own node.
18	
19	This split lets sensing (detector nodes) and actuation (guitar nodes) live on separate nodes
20	of one PLCA bus, with marvin selecting the active one of each class (see top-level
21	[`SPEC.md`](../../SPEC.md) §2 "Node classes"). Multiple guitar variants may coexist on the bus.
22	
23	The actuation logic is a direct port of fretboard's [`cmd_receive.c`](../fretboard/cmd_receive.c)
24	(bitmask → open-drain assert / tri-state release) — it has no detector dependencies. fretboard
25	keeps actuating until this node is proven; marvin flips its command target then.
26	
27	## 2. Hardware
28	
29	| Spec | Value |
30	|------|-------|
31	| Device | PIC32CM PL10 (same family as fretboard; Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz) |
32	| Toolchain | XC32 |
33	| MAC-PHY | LAN8651 (10BASE-T1S), SPI Mode 0, ≤ ~12 MHz on the 24 MHz part |
34	
35	**To be fixed when the guitar MCC project is generated** (Greg, in MPLAB — same shape as
36	marvin's FLEXCOM4 setup):
37	
38	- One SERCOM in **SPI-master mode** (Mode 0: CPOL=0/CPHA=0, MSB first) for the LAN8651, plus
39	  GPIO for `CS_N` (hardware SS if held across a transaction, else bit-banged), `IRQ_N`
40	  (external-interrupt pin), and `RST`.
41	- Seven **open-drain** button-output GPIOs (assert = drive low, release = input/tri-state so the
42	  controller's pull-up restores idle), bit layout matching the wire command:
43	
44	  | Bit | Output |
45	  |----:|--------|
46	  | 0 | Green fret |
47	  | 1 | Red fret |
48	  | 2 | Yellow fret |
49	  | 3 | Blue fret |
50	  | 4 | Orange fret |
51	  | 5 | Strum down |
52	  | 6 | Strum up |
53	
54	- A periodic timer (TC) tick to service the bus / apply commands (no 240 Hz ADC scan — that's
55	  the detector's job).
56	
57	PoDL on the pair powers the node (transparent to firmware; see [T1S/PoDL link](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md) §6).
58	
59	## 3. The T1S link
60	
61	A **PLCA follower** — the mirror of marvin's coordinator glue, reusing the shared
62	[`third_party/oa-tc6-lib`](../../third_party/oa-tc6-lib) and the same L2 framing:
63	
64	- **Node id 2**, MAC `02:00:00:00:00:02` (addressing scheme: [T1S/PoDL link](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md) §7.1).
65	- `TC6_Init` + `TC6Regs_Init(enablePlca=true, nodeId=2, nodeCount=8, …)` — follower, **not**
66	  coordinator.
67	- Custom ethertype `0x88B5`; marvin's command rides as a 1-byte payload inside the 14-byte
68	  Ethernet header. The guitar accepts frames addressed to its MAC from the coordinator.
69	- **Bare-metal** (no FreeRTOS on PL10): the TC6 service loop runs from the main loop / timer
70	  tick, not a task; `IRQ_N` is wired to a SERCOM-EIC pin (not a PIO controller as on marvin).
71	
72	The marvin-side reference for all of this is [`firmware/marvin/default/src/net/t1s/t1s_link.c`](../marvin/default/src/net/t1s/t1s_link.c)
73	(coordinator) — the follower inverts the roles: RX the command, no detector-stream TX.
74	
75	## 4. Firmware design (to build)
76	
77	1. **Bring-up:** reset the LAN8651 (`RST` pulse), configure SPI (Mode 0), `TC6_Init` +
78	   `TC6Regs_Init` as follower id 2. Gate: read chip revision + PLCA *follower* status.
79	2. **RX path:** TC6 delivers the marvin command frame → validate ethertype `0x88B5` → take the
80	   1-byte payload as the button bitmask → apply to the 7 GPIOs (port fretboard's
81	   `cmd_receive_apply_mask` logic).
82	3. **TX path:** none required initially. Optional `applied_mask` telemetry back to marvin (for
83	   edge-ai zero-skew labels) is **deferred** with the edge-ai re-homing effort.
84	4. **Service:** call `TC6_Service` from the main loop / tick, woken by `IRQ_N`.
85	5. **CLI** (debug aid, on the SERCOM1 UART via embedded-cli, static allocation): `t1s` (link /
86	   sync / chipRev / PLCA / counters), `btn <mask>` and `tap <mask> [ms]` drive the button GPIOs
87	   directly — so the Wii-guitar wiring can be exercised before the T1S link is up.
88	
89	## 5. What this is *not*
90	
91	- **Not a sensor.** No phototransistors, no ADC — sensing is the detector node's job.
92	- **Not an on-device model.** The edge-ai MODEL_DRIVEN inference stays on fretboard for now;
93	  re-homing it (detector infers → T1S → guitar) is out of scope.
94	- **Not a game brain.** No chord/strum timing — marvin's timing pipeline owns that and sends
95	  the resulting bitmask.
96	- **Not the PLCA coordinator.** marvin (node 0) beacons the cycle; guitar is a follower.
97	
98	## 6. Milestones
99	
100	| Status | Item |
101	|---|---|
102	| ✅ | **G0** — guitar MCC project: SERCOM0 SPI (Mode 0), EIC EXTINT13 (falling) on `IRQ_N`=PA13, `CS`=PA15 / `RST`=PA14 GPIO, 7 button GPIOs, SERCOM1 debug UART (CS/IRQ_N reassigned to match wiring) |
103	| ✅ | **G1** — T1S follower bring-up on hardware: `LAN8651 up - chipRev=2 … PLCA follower id=2/8` |
104	| ✅ | **G2** — end-to-end: marvin's command over T1S → the addressed Wii GPIO asserts |
105	| ✅ | **CLI** — `t1s`/`btn`/`tap`/`id`/`plca` on the debug UART (embedded-cli). Drives the Wii-guitar GPIOs locally and reports T1S link/sync/PLCA status. |
106	| ✅ | **Heartbeat** — periodic presence frame (ethertype `0x88B6`) to the coordinator so marvin's `nodes` shows this node present |
107	| 🔭 | **G3** — full system: `fretboard` (detector) + `guitar` (actuator) both on the bus with marvin selecting the active of each (marvin already targets the guitar; needs the fretboard moved to T1S) |
108
```

```text
1	# edge-ai
2	
3	Distill marvin's emitted gameplay commands into a small causal model over the
4	fretboard's 5-channel ADC stream. **Design + plan live in [`docs/`](docs/)** —
5	start with [`docs/SPEC.md`](docs/SPEC.md) and [`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md).
6	
7	This package is the host-side pipeline (PyTorch): train a causal CNN, then int8
8	post-training quantise it into the `model_weights.h` the fretboard firmware runs.
9	Input is the actuator-labelled CSV from `marvin-perf export-ml --labels=actuator-fb`.
10	
11	## Layout
12	
13	- `edge_ai/data.py` — CSV loader + causal row-index windowing (stdlib).
14	- `edge_ai/lag.py` — photo-dip → strum lag measurement (stdlib).
15	- `edge_ai/metrics.py` — per-bit accuracy/F1 + strum-event timing (stdlib).
16	- `edge_ai/model.py` — causal 1D-CNN (`StrumNet`, torch).
17	- `edge_ai/train.py` — training loop + holdout evaluation (torch).
18	- `edge_ai/quantize.py` — int8 post-training quantiser + `model_weights.h` emitter (numpy/torch).
19	- `edge_ai/viz.py` — torchinfo summary, torchview graph, receptive-field cone plot (`viz` group).
20	- `edge_ai/cli.py` — `edge-ai {lag,train,eval,quantize,viz}`.
21	
22	The stdlib pieces (`data`, `lag`, `metrics`) run without numpy/torch; only
23	`model`/`train`/`eval` need the `train` dependency group.
24	
25	## Use
26	
27	```sh
28	export UV_CACHE_DIR="$TMPDIR/uv-cache"   # only needed inside a restricted sandbox
29	
30	# size the causal window from real data (no torch needed)
31	uv run edge-ai lag path/to/song-expert.csv --curve
32	
33	# install the heavy deps and train
34	uv sync --group train --group dev
35	uv run edge-ai train --holdout heldout.csv song1.csv song2.csv song3.csv \
36	    --window 60 --out model.pt
37	uv run edge-ai eval --model model.pt heldout.csv
38	
39	# int8 quantise -> firmware header (deploy model: --no-holdout --channels 16 --window 85)
40	uv run edge-ai quantize --model model.pt --name hard \
41	    --strum-thresh 0.80 --out ../../firmware/fretboard/model_weights.h song1.csv song2.csv
42	
43	# visualise the model (summary + RF cone always; graph needs the graphviz binary)
44	uv sync --group train --group viz   # adds torchinfo, torchview, matplotlib
45	uv run edge-ai viz --model model.pt --rf-cone rf_cone.png --graph graph.svg
46	
47	# tests (stdlib-only; needs the dev group for pytest)
48	uv run --group dev pytest
49	```
50	
51	For block diagrams beyond these, export the float model to ONNX and open it in
52	[Netron](https://netron.app), or redraw in PlotNeuralNet / NN-SVG.
53	
54	Corpus is Expert-only, one song held out — see [`docs/training.md`](docs/training.md) §4.
55
```

```text
1	# gameplay — GH3 game-state engine (offline prototype)
2	
3	Host-side prototype for marvin's game-state observer/controller (spec §4.8, milestone
4	M9/M10). Algorithms are proven here against the real-screen corpus, then the proven,
5	simple logic ports to a firmware `gameplay_engine` module. See
6	[`docs/journal.md`](docs/journal.md) and `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`.
7	
8	So far:
9	- **Screen classifier** — which GH3 screen is this (`main_menu`, `song_select`, `in_song`,
10	  …) or `UNKNOWN`.
11	- **Static-list selection reader** — within a recognized static-list screen, which menu
12	  item is highlighted.
13	- **song_select reader** — which song is in the highlight slot (and which setlist).
14	- **Navigator (M10)** — plan a high-level verb (practice-run a song on a difficulty) and
15	  execute it closed-loop along the menu graph, verified against a simulated menu and the real
16	  observer.
17	
18	## Screen classifier
19	
20	Coarse **fixed-region colour fingerprint** + **nearest-centroid** classifier with an
21	**UNKNOWN reject** rule (Q10: fixed-region matching, not general CV). A frame is split
22	into a `cols×rows` grid; each region collapses to its mean BGR; the concatenated vector
23	is compared by integer L1 distance to one centroid per screen class. The design is shaped
24	to port to cheap integer C and is **memory-bound, not compute-bound** on the SAM9X75.
25	
26	Two knobs (chosen empirically by `gameplay eval`, defaults baked into `FingerprintConfig`):
27	
28	- **sample density** — dense (every pixel; ~7–20 ms on-device) vs a sparse N×N lattice per
29	  region (sub-millisecond). Default: 5×5 lattice.
30	- **normalization** — per-frame value standardization, which cancels the **gain/offset
31	  value-slop** of the Wii's analog-component → HDMI path. Default: on (it is what lifts
32	  slop-robustness to ~99.8%).
33	
34	Default config (12×8, 5×5 samples, normalized): 96% leave-one-out accuracy (= 100% of all
35	multi-sample classes; the 4 single-sample classes can't be LOO-matched), ~99.8% robustness
36	across the synthetic analog-slop envelope, ~0.1–0.4 ms estimated per classification.
37	
38	## Static-list selection reader
39	
40	For the 8 fixed-count static-list screens, per-screen menu metadata (ordered items +
41	menu-band geometry, in `metadata.py`) divides the band into one cell per item. The selected
42	cell is the one that deviates most from its **unselected baseline** (learned per screen from
43	the corpus) — GH3 marks selection by *changing* a row (colour/bar), not by making it
44	brightest, so "what changed" is the robust signal. Cell colours are normalized per frame to
45	cancel gain/offset slop. Result: 100% clean / ~99.4% slop on the 33 labelled frames.
46	
47	## song_select reader
48	
49	The selected song sits in a fixed highlight slot (except each setlist's first song, which
50	sits one row lower). We identify it by matching the slot's low-res grayscale bitmap against
51	the 64 per-song templates — across **both** setlists, so main/bonus falls out of the match.
52	A small read-time offset search re-aligns the slot, which makes the fine grid tolerant of
53	positional slop. Result: 64/64 clean, ~99.1% under slop. The active setlist is also read
54	independently from the page background colour (main = yellow, bonus = white; warmth R−B):
55	100% clean and under slop.
56	
57	Char-level OCR is deliberately out of scope: menu items and song titles are a closed set we
58	already have reference bitmaps for (match, don't decode); digit OCR comes only with score
59	reading. `section_select` (variable list) and reading the scrolling neighbour list are deferred.
60	
61	## Navigator (M10)
62	
63	`navgraph.py` encodes the menu graph (`firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`) as data;
64	`navigator.py` plans a verb (`plan_practice_run`, `plan_goto`) and runs it closed-loop through
65	an `Observer`/`Actuator` seam. The controller is observation-driven — each step runs against
66	the screen actually observed — which yields normal progress, the `part_select` skip, and RED
67	recovery from one rule. Offline it's driven by `simgame.py` (the test oracle); on the device
68	the same seam takes the CV observer + fretboard link. Selections strum the signed delta from
69	the observed cursor (sticky-safe); FULL SONG/FULL SPEED strum up until the selection stops
70	moving (no blind count).
71	
72	## Usage
73	
74	```sh
75	uv sync --group dev
76	
77	uv run gameplay eval                 # classifier + selection reader: accuracy, robustness, thresholds, HW time
78	uv run gameplay eval --no-sweep      # skip the parameter sweep
79	uv run gameplay classify path/to/frame.png   # screen id (+ selection / song)
80	uv run gameplay rows path/to/frame.png       # debug per-cell selection scores
81	uv run gameplay navigate --song 19 --difficulty hard   # plan + run a practice run vs the sim
82	uv run gameplay export-c --out gameplay_metadata.h     # freeze recognizer metadata to a C header
83	
84	uv run pytest
85	```
86	
87	## Firmware port (marvin `gameplay_engine`, spec §4.8)
88	
89	The proven algorithms are being ported to marvin firmware in phases (see `docs/journal.md`).
90	Phase 0 (done) is `gameplay export-c`: it emits all recognizer data — classifier
91	centroids/thresholds, static-list menu geometry + baselines, song templates/ROIs — as a single
92	generated C header (`gameplay_metadata.h`, plain PODs + flat arrays) that the firmware compiles
93	in. Floats are only the per-frame-normalized baselines/song vectors (soft-float on the ARM926).
94	The generated header is verified to compile under `cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra`.
95	
96	The corpus is read from `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/` (override with
97	`$GAMEPLAY_CORPUS_DIR`). Labels come from each filename's prefix.
98
```
</details></tool-use>

firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md:- **Fretboard → marvin:** raw ADC stream (5 channels × 16-bit) at 240 Hz, in a 17-byte start/end-bracketed frame (`0x03 … 0xFC`, with `sample_seq` + `applied_mask`). The FLEXCOM1 RX ring fills continuously from its ISR; a persistent read-threshold notification wakes `fretboard_rx_task`, which drains the ring, resyncs on the frame markers, and republishes each valid frame as a `PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW` perf-log record (default-disabled, host enables via `PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK`). This is the on-board capture path until the SD-card recorder lands; it's also the substrate for the future `adc_fretboard` detector (§4.2).

firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md:| 2026-06-03 | Data-stream frame grows 12→17 bytes: `0x03 \| g r y b o (5×u16 LE) \| sample_seq (u32 LE) \| applied_mask (u8) \| 0xFC`. `sample_seq` is a monotonic counter incremented once per tick in `data_stream_send` (before the TX-buffer check, so a dropped send shows as a gap); `applied_mask` comes from a new `cmd_receive_current_mask()` getter. Resolves open-questions #3 and #4. | Closes the edge-ai data-sync hole (edge-ai journal 2026-06-03). Pairing the actuator state with the ADC scan *in the same frame* makes label↔feature alignment atomic at the source, instead of marvin reconstructing it across its bursty USB RX and separate TX clocks — which Phase-2 training showed floored strum timing at ~20 ms. The seq counter lets the host reconstruct true 240 Hz ordering and detect dropped frames. Callback order is scan→send→receive, so `current_mask` at send time is exactly the state driven *during* this scan. Wire-format break: requires marvin's RX parser + `perf_rec_fretboard_raw_t` (schema v4) to update in lockstep. 17 B × 240 Hz = 4.08 KB/s, still ~12× under the 500 000-baud budget. |
firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md:| 2026-06-02 | SERCOM1 baud raised to 500 000 (was lower). | At 240 Hz × 12-byte TX frames + sporadic RX command bytes, 500 000 baud (≈ 50 000 B/s usable) gives ~17× headroom over the 2 880 B/s steady-state — plenty for jitter and back-pressure without flow control. |
firmware/fretboard/docs/journal.md:1. **No corruption signalling on the wire.** A bit-flip inside the 5 uint16 payload bytes is silently accepted — only out-of-range start/end bytes are caught. 177:| **(optional) dev PC** | Calibration / training-data ingest / replay viewer + operator console | SD card swap (primary), USB CDC for perf-log, and the FLEXCOM2 serial console (115 200 8N1, via an FTDI channel) for interactive control (§4.9). No runtime dependency. |
190:| FLEXCOM2 (USART) | ✅ in use | Operator command console — 115 200 Bd 8N1, ring-buffer mode (§4.9). |
199:| Free FLEXCOMs | several available | FLEXCOM1 = fretboard link (§4.3), FLEXCOM2 = console (§4.9), FLEXCOM8 = I²C; others remain free. |
275:Direct **FLEXCOM1 USART** link between marvin and the fretboard MCU — a plain UART wire, no USB. marvin's `PA28` (FLEXCOM1_IO0, `GUITAR_TX`) and `PA29` (FLEXCOM1_IO1, `GUITAR_RX`) connect to the fretboard's SERCOM1 (`PB01` RX / `PB00` TX). Both ends run **500 000 baud, 8N1**. The FLEXCOM1 USART runs in Harmony ring-buffer mode so RX never drops bytes between reads. (Was FLEXCOM2 until the console moved onto FLEXCOM2 — see §4.9.)
457:An **interactive text console** over **FLEXCOM2 USART (115 200 8N1, ring-buffer mode)** — marvin's `PA13` (FLEXCOM2_IO0, `CLI_TX`) / `PA14` (FLEXCOM2_IO1, `CLI_RX`) — deliberately on a separate channel from the DBGU log/printf chatter — log output stays on DBGU, console I/O stays on FLEXCOM2, so neither pollutes the other.
461:- **Mechanics:** one FreeRTOS task drains the FLEXCOM2 RX ring (woken by a 1-byte read-threshold notification, like `fretboard_rx_task`), feeds bytes to embedded-cli, and runs the dispatcher. Output is written byte-by-byte into the TX ring.
```

1	# Fretboard Firmware Specification
2	
3	> **Re-scoped to a T1S sense+actuate node (2026-06-17):** the fretboard is a 10BASE-T1S
4	> PLCA follower (id 1) that infers actuator commands from the phototransistor data and drives the
5	> [`guitar`](../guitar/SPEC.md) node over T1S, while also streaming its data to marvin. The old UART
6	> link, the standalone Wii-guitar GPIO outputs (`cmd_receive.c`), and the `FRETBOARD_LINK`/`FRETBOARD_MODE`
7	> build flags are gone — one behaviour. Node-class model: top-level [`SPEC.md`](../../SPEC.md) §2; link
8	> detail: [`docs/t1s-podl-link.md`](../../docs/t1s-podl-link.md).
9	
10	## Overview
11	
12	Firmware for PIC32CM6408PL10048 (Cortex-M0+, 24 MHz). The fretboard is a 10BASE-T1S
13	node that both **senses** and **drives**. Each 240 Hz tick it samples five
14	phototransistors above the TV strike line; an on-device int8 neural net
15	(`model_infer.c`, weights in the generated `model_weights.h`) infers the Wii-guitar
16	button bitmask from the ADC window. Over T1S it then:
